#!/bin/sh
#
# An example hook script to check the commit log message taken by
# applypatch from an e-mail message.
#
# The hook should exit with non-zero status after issuing an
# appropriate message if it wants to stop the commit.  The hook is
# allowed to edit the commit message file.
#
# To enable this hook, rename this file to "applypatch-msg".

. git-sh-setup

test -x "$commitmsg" && exec "$commitmsg" ${1+"$@"}
:

<file path=".git/hooks/commit-msg.sample">
#!/bin/sh
#
# An example hook script to check the commit log message.
# Called by "git commit" with one argument, the name of the file
# that has the commit message.  The hook should exit with non-zero
# status after issuing an appropriate message if it wants to stop the
# commit.  The hook is allowed to edit the commit message file.
#
# To enable this hook, rename this file to "commit-msg".

# Uncomment the below to add a Signed-off-by line to the message.
# Doing this in a hook is a bad idea in general, but the prepare-commit-msg
# hook is more suited to it.
#
# SOB=$(git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT | sed -n 's/^\(.*>\).*$/Signed-off-by: \1/p')
# grep -qs "^$SOB" "$1" || echo "$SOB" >> "$1"

# This example catches duplicate Signed-off-by lines and messages that
# would confuse 'git am'.

ret=0

test "" = "$(grep '^Signed-off-by: ' "$1" |
	 sort | uniq -c | sed -e '/^[ 	]*1[ 	]/d')" || {
	echo >&2 Duplicate Signed-off-by lines.
	ret=1
}

comment_re="$(
	{
		git config --get-regexp "^core\.comment(char|string)\$" ||
			echo '#'
	} | sed -n -e '
		${
			s/^[^ ]* //
			s|[][*./\]|\\&|g
			s/^auto$/[#;@!$%^&|:]/
			p
		}'
)"
scissors_line="^${comment_re} -\{8,\} >8 -\{8,\}\$"
comment_line="^${comment_re}.*"
blank_line='^[ 	]*$'
# Disallow lines starting with "diff -" or "Index: " in the body of the
# message. Stop looking if we see a scissors line.
line="$(sed -n -e "
	# Skip comments and blank lines at the start of the file.
	/${scissors_line}/q
	/${comment_line}/d
	/${blank_line}/d
	# The first paragraph will become the subject header so
	# does not need to be checked.
	: subject
	n
	/${scissors_line}/q
	/${blank_line}/!b subject
	# Check the body of the message for problematic
	# prefixes.
	: body
	n
	/${scissors_line}/q
	/${comment_line}/b body
	/^diff -/{p;q;}
	/^Index: /{p;q;}
	b body
	" "$1")"
if test -n "$line"
then
	echo >&2 "Message contains a diff that will confuse 'git am'."
	echo >&2 "To fix this indent the diff."
	ret=1
fi

exit $ret
</file>

<file path=".git/hooks/fsmonitor-watchman.sample">
#!/usr/bin/perl

use strict;
use warnings;
use IPC::Open2;

# An example hook script to integrate Watchman
# (https://facebook.github.io/watchman/) with git to speed up detecting
# new and modified files.
#
# The hook is passed a version (currently 2) and last update token
# formatted as a string and outputs to stdout a new update token and
# all files that have been modified since the update token. Paths must
# be relative to the root of the working tree and separated by a single NUL.
#
# To enable this hook, rename this file to "query-watchman" and set
# 'git config core.fsmonitor .git/hooks/query-watchman'
#
my ($version, $last_update_token) = @ARGV;

# Uncomment for debugging
# print STDERR "$0 $version $last_update_token\n";

# Check the hook interface version
if ($version ne 2) {
	die "Unsupported query-fsmonitor hook version '$version'.\n" .
	    "Falling back to scanning...\n";
}

my $git_work_tree = get_working_dir();

my $json_pkg;
eval {
	require JSON::XS;
	$json_pkg = "JSON::XS";
	1;
} or do {
	require JSON::PP;
	$json_pkg = "JSON::PP";
};

launch_watchman();

sub launch_watchman {
	my $o = watchman_query();
	if (is_work_tree_watched($o)) {
		output_result($o->{clock}, @{$o->{files}});
	}
}

sub output_result {
	my ($clockid, @files) = @_;

	# Uncomment for debugging watchman output
	# open (my $fh, ">", ".git/watchman-output.out");
	# binmode $fh, ":utf8";
	# print $fh "$clockid\n@files\n";
	# close $fh;

	binmode STDOUT, ":utf8";
	print $clockid;
	print "\0";
	local $, = "\0";
	print @files;
}

sub watchman_clock {
	my $response = qx/watchman clock "$git_work_tree"/;
	die "Failed to get clock id on '$git_work_tree'.\n" .
		"Falling back to scanning...\n" if $? != 0;

	return $json_pkg->new->utf8->decode($response);
}

sub watchman_query {
	my $pid = open2(\*CHLD_OUT, \*CHLD_IN, 'watchman -j --no-pretty')
	or die "open2() failed: $!\n" .
	"Falling back to scanning...\n";

	# In the query expression below we're asking for names of files that
	# changed since $last_update_token but not from the .git folder.
	#
	# To accomplish this, we're using the "since" generator to use the
	# recency index to select candidate nodes and "fields" to limit the
	# output to file names only. Then we're using the "expression" term to
	# further constrain the results.
	my $last_update_line = "";
	if (substr($last_update_token, 0, 1) eq "c") {
		$last_update_token = "\"$last_update_token\"";
		$last_update_line = qq[\n"since": $last_update_token,];
	}
	my $query = <<"	END";
		["query", "$git_work_tree", {$last_update_line
			"fields": ["name"],
			"expression": ["not", ["dirname", ".git"]]
		}]
	END

	# Uncomment for debugging the watchman query
	# open (my $fh, ">", ".git/watchman-query.json");
	# print $fh $query;
	# close $fh;

	print CHLD_IN $query;
	close CHLD_IN;
	my $response = do {local $/; <CHLD_OUT>};

	# Uncomment for debugging the watch response
	# open ($fh, ">", ".git/watchman-response.json");
	# print $fh $response;
	# close $fh;

	die "Watchman: command returned no output.\n" .
	"Falling back to scanning...\n" if $response eq "";
	die "Watchman: command returned invalid output: $response\n" .
	"Falling back to scanning...\n" unless $response =~ /^\{/;

	return $json_pkg->new->utf8->decode($response);
}

sub is_work_tree_watched {
	my ($output) = @_;
	my $error = $output->{error};
	if ($error and $error =~ m/unable to resolve root .* directory (.*) is not watched/) {
		my $response = qx/watchman watch "$git_work_tree"/;
		die "Failed to make watchman watch '$git_work_tree'.\n" .
		    "Falling back to scanning...\n" if $? != 0;
		$output = $json_pkg->new->utf8->decode($response);
		$error = $output->{error};
		die "Watchman: $error.\n" .
		"Falling back to scanning...\n" if $error;

		# Uncomment for debugging watchman output
		# open (my $fh, ">", ".git/watchman-output.out");
		# close $fh;

		# Watchman will always return all files on the first query so
		# return the fast "everything is dirty" flag to git and do the
		# Watchman query just to get it over with now so we won't pay
		# the cost in git to look up each individual file.
		my $o = watchman_clock();
		$error = $o->{error};

		die "Watchman: $error.\n" .
		"Falling back to scanning...\n" if $error;

		output_result($o->{clock}, ("/"));
		return 0;
	}

	die "Watchman: $error.\n" .
	"Falling back to scanning...\n" if $error;

	return 1;
}

sub get_working_dir {
	my $working_dir;
	if ($^O =~ 'msys' || $^O =~ 'cygwin') {
		$working_dir = Win32::GetCwd();
		$working_dir =~ tr/\\/\//;
	} else {
		require Cwd;
		$working_dir = Cwd::cwd();
	}

	return $working_dir;
}
</file>

<file path=".git/hooks/pre-commit.sample">
#!/bin/sh
#
# An example hook script to verify what is about to be committed.
# Called by "git commit" with no arguments.  The hook should
# exit with non-zero status after issuing an appropriate message if
# it wants to stop the commit.
#
# To enable this hook, rename this file to "pre-commit".

if git rev-parse --verify HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1
then
	against=HEAD
else
	# Initial commit: diff against an empty tree object
	against=$(git hash-object -t tree /dev/null)
fi

# If you want to allow non-ASCII filenames set this variable to true.
allownonascii=$(git config --type=bool hooks.allownonascii)

# Redirect output to stderr.
exec 1>&2

# Cross platform projects tend to avoid non-ASCII filenames; prevent
# them from being added to the repository. We exploit the fact that the
# printable range starts at the space character and ends with tilde.
if [ "$allownonascii" != "true" ] &&
	# Note that the use of brackets around a tr range is ok here, (it's
	# even required, for portability to Solaris 10's /usr/bin/tr), since
	# the square bracket bytes happen to fall in the designated range.
	test $(git diff-index --cached --name-only --diff-filter=A -z $against |
	  LC_ALL=C tr -d '[ -~]\0' | wc -c) != 0
then
	cat <<\EOF
Error: Attempt to add a non-ASCII file name.

This can cause problems if you want to work with people on other platforms.

To be portable it is advisable to rename the file.

If you know what you are doing you can disable this check using:

  git config hooks.allownonascii true
EOF
	exit 1
fi

# If there are whitespace errors, print the offending file names and fail.
exec git diff-index --check --cached $against --
</file>

<file path=".git/hooks/pre-merge-commit.sample">
#!/bin/sh
#
# An example hook script to verify what is about to be committed.
# Called by "git merge" with no arguments.  The hook should
# exit with non-zero status after issuing an appropriate message to

. git-sh-setup

        exec "$GIT_DIR/hooks/pre-commit"

<file path=".git/hooks/pre-push.sample">
#!/bin/sh

# An example hook script to verify what is about to be pushed.  Called by "git
# push" after it has checked the remote status, but before anything has been
# pushed.  If this script exits with a non-zero status nothing will be pushed.
#
# This hook is called with the following parameters:
#
# $1 -- Name of the remote to which the push is being done
# $2 -- URL to which the push is being done
#
# If pushing without using a named remote those arguments will be equal.
#
# Information about the commits which are being pushed is supplied as lines to
# the standard input in the form:
#
#   <local ref> <local oid> <remote ref> <remote oid>
#
# This sample shows how to prevent push of commits where the log message starts
# with "WIP" (work in progress).

remote="$1"
url="$2"

zero=$(git hash-object --stdin </dev/null | tr '[0-9a-f]' '0')

while read local_ref local_oid remote_ref remote_oid
do
	if test "$local_oid" = "$zero"
	then
		# Handle delete
		:
	else
		if test "$remote_oid" = "$zero"
		then
			# New branch, examine all commits
			range="$local_oid"
		else
			# Update to existing branch, examine new commits
			range="$remote_oid..$local_oid"
		fi

		# Check for WIP commit
		commit=$(git rev-list -n 1 --grep '^WIP' "$range")
		if test -n "$commit"
		then
			echo >&2 "Found WIP commit in $local_ref, not pushing"
			exit 1
		fi
	fi
done

exit 0
</file>

<file path=".git/hooks/pre-rebase.sample">
#!/bin/sh
#
# Copyright (c) 2006, 2008 Junio C Hamano
#
# The "pre-rebase" hook is run just before "git rebase" starts doing
# its job, and can prevent the command from running by exiting with
# non-zero status.
#
# The hook is called with the following parameters:
#
# $1 -- the upstream the series was forked from.
# $2 -- the branch being rebased (or empty when rebasing the current branch).
#
# This sample shows how to prevent topic branches that are already
# merged to 'next' branch from getting rebased, because allowing it
# would result in rebasing already published history.

publish=next
basebranch="$1"
if test "$#" = 2
then
	topic="refs/heads/$2"
else
	topic=`git symbolic-ref HEAD` ||
	exit 0 ;# we do not interrupt rebasing detached HEAD
fi

case "$topic" in
refs/heads/??/*)
	;;
*)
	exit 0 ;# we do not interrupt others.
	;;
esac

# Now we are dealing with a topic branch being rebased
# on top of master.  Is it OK to rebase it?

# Does the topic really exist?
git show-ref -q "$topic" || {
	echo >&2 "No such branch $topic"
	exit 1
}

# Is topic fully merged to master?
not_in_master=`git rev-list --pretty=oneline ^master "$topic"`
if test -z "$not_in_master"
then
	echo >&2 "$topic is fully merged to master; better remove it."
	exit 1 ;# we could allow it, but there is no point.
fi

# Is topic ever merged to next?  If so you should not be rebasing it.
only_next_1=`git rev-list ^master "^$topic" ${publish} | sort`
only_next_2=`git rev-list ^master           ${publish} | sort`
if test "$only_next_1" = "$only_next_2"
then
	not_in_topic=`git rev-list "^$topic" master`
	if test -z "$not_in_topic"
	then
		echo >&2 "$topic is already up to date with master"
		exit 1 ;# we could allow it, but there is no point.
	else
		exit 0
	fi
else
	not_in_next=`git rev-list --pretty=oneline ^${publish} "$topic"`
	/usr/bin/perl -e '
		my $topic = $ARGV[0];
		my $msg = "* $topic has commits already merged to public branch:\n";
		my (%not_in_next) = map {
			/^([0-9a-f]+) /;
			($1 => 1);
		} split(/\n/, $ARGV[1]);
		for my $elem (map {
				/^([0-9a-f]+) (.*)$/;
				[$1 => $2];
			} split(/\n/, $ARGV[2])) {
			if (!exists $not_in_next{$elem->[0]}) {
				if ($msg) {
					print STDERR $msg;
					undef $msg;
				}
				print STDERR " $elem->[1]\n";
			}
		}
	' "$topic" "$not_in_next" "$not_in_master"
	exit 1
fi

<<\DOC_END

This sample hook safeguards topic branches that have been
published from being rewound.

The workflow assumed here is:

 * Once a topic branch forks from "master", "master" is never
   merged into it again (either directly or indirectly).

 * Once a topic branch is fully cooked and merged into "master",
   it is deleted.  If you need to build on top of it to correct
   earlier mistakes, a new topic branch is created by forking at
   the tip of the "master".  This is not strictly necessary, but
   it makes it easier to keep your history simple.

 * Whenever you need to test or publish your changes to topic
   branches, merge them into "next" branch.

The script, being an example, hardcodes the publish branch name
to be "next", but it is trivial to make it configurable via
$GIT_DIR/config mechanism.

With this workflow, you would want to know:

(1) ... if a topic branch has ever been merged to "next".  Young
    topic branches can have stupid mistakes you would rather
    clean up before publishing, and things that have not been
    merged into other branches can be easily rebased without
    affecting other people.  But once it is published, you would
    not want to rewind it.

(2) ... if a topic branch has been fully merged to "master".
    Then you can delete it.  More importantly, you should not
    build on top of it -- other people may already want to
    change things related to the topic as patches against your
    "master", so if you need further changes, it is better to
    fork the topic (perhaps with the same name) afresh from the
    tip of "master".

Let's look at this example:

		   o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o "next"
		  /       /           /           /
		 /   a---a---b A     /           /
		/   /               /           /
	       /   /   c---c---c---c B         /
	      /   /   /             \         /
	     /   /   /   b---b C     \       /
	    /   /   /   /             \     /
    ---o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o "master"


A, B and C are topic branches.

 * A has one fix since it was merged up to "next".

 * B has finished.  It has been fully merged up to "master" and "next",
   and is ready to be deleted.

 * C has not merged to "next" at all.

We would want to allow C to be rebased, refuse A, and encourage
B to be deleted.

To compute (1):

	git rev-list ^master ^topic next
	git rev-list ^master        next

	if these match, topic has not merged in next at all.

To compute (2):

	git rev-list master..topic

	if this is empty, it is fully merged to "master".

DOC_END
</file>

<file path=".git/hooks/pre-receive.sample">
#!/bin/sh
#
# An example hook script to make use of push options.
# The example simply echoes all push options that start with 'echoback='
# and rejects all pushes when the "reject" push option is used.
#
# To enable this hook, rename this file to "pre-receive".

if test -n "$GIT_PUSH_OPTION_COUNT"
then
	i=0
	while test "$i" -lt "$GIT_PUSH_OPTION_COUNT"
	do
		eval "value=\$GIT_PUSH_OPTION_$i"
		case "$value" in
		echoback=*)
			echo "echo from the pre-receive-hook: ${value#*=}" >&2
			;;
		reject)
			exit 1
		esac
		i=$((i + 1))
	done
fi
</file>

<file path=".git/hooks/push-to-checkout.sample">
#!/bin/sh

# An example hook script to update a checked-out tree on a git push.
#
# This hook is invoked by git-receive-pack(1) when it reacts to git
# push and updates reference(s) in its repository, and when the push
# tries to update the branch that is currently checked out and the
# receive.denyCurrentBranch configuration variable is set to
# updateInstead.
#
# By default, such a push is refused if the working tree and the index
# of the remote repository has any difference from the currently
# checked out commit; when both the working tree and the index match
# the current commit, they are updated to match the newly pushed tip
# of the branch. This hook is to be used to override the default
# behaviour; however the code below reimplements the default behaviour
# as a starting point for convenient modification.
#
# The hook receives the commit with which the tip of the current
# branch is going to be updated:
commit=$1

# It can exit with a non-zero status to refuse the push (when it does
# so, it must not modify the index or the working tree).
die () {
	echo >&2 "$*"
	exit 1
}

# Or it can make any necessary changes to the working tree and to the
# index to bring them to the desired state when the tip of the current
# branch is updated to the new commit, and exit with a zero status.
#
# For example, the hook can simply run git read-tree -u -m HEAD "$1"
# in order to emulate git fetch that is run in the reverse direction
# with git push, as the two-tree form of git read-tree -u -m is
# essentially the same as git switch or git checkout that switches
# branches while keeping the local changes in the working tree that do
# not interfere with the difference between the branches.

# The below is a more-or-less exact translation to shell of the C code
# for the default behaviour for git's push-to-checkout hook defined in
# the push_to_deploy() function in builtin/receive-pack.c.
#
# Note that the hook will be executed from the repository directory,
# not from the working tree, so if you want to perform operations on
# the working tree, you will have to adapt your code accordingly, e.g.
# by adding "cd .." or using relative paths.

if ! git update-index -q --ignore-submodules --refresh
then
	die "Up-to-date check failed"
fi

if ! git diff-files --quiet --ignore-submodules --
then
	die "Working directory has unstaged changes"
fi

# This is a rough translation of:
#
#   head_has_history() ? "HEAD" : EMPTY_TREE_SHA1_HEX
if git cat-file -e HEAD 2>/dev/null
then
	head=HEAD
else
	head=$(git hash-object -t tree --stdin </dev/null)
fi

if ! git diff-index --quiet --cached --ignore-submodules $head --
then
	die "Working directory has staged changes"
fi

if ! git read-tree -u -m "$commit"
then
	die "Could not update working tree to new HEAD"
fi
</file>

<file path=".git/hooks/sendemail-validate.sample">
#!/bin/sh

# An example hook script to validate a patch (and/or patch series) before
# sending it via email.
#
# The hook should exit with non-zero status after issuing an appropriate
# message if it wants to prevent the email(s) from being sent.
#
# To enable this hook, rename this file to "sendemail-validate".
#
# By default, it will only check that the patch(es) can be applied on top of
# the default upstream branch without conflicts in a secondary worktree. After
# validation (successful or not) of the last patch of a series, the worktree
# will be deleted.
#
# The following config variables can be set to change the default remote and
# remote ref that are used to apply the patches against:
#
#   sendemail.validateRemote (default: origin)
#   sendemail.validateRemoteRef (default: HEAD)
#
# Replace the TODO placeholders with appropriate checks according to your
# needs.

validate_cover_letter () {
	file="$1"
	# TODO: Replace with appropriate checks (e.g. spell checking).
	true
}

validate_patch () {
	file="$1"
	# Ensure that the patch applies without conflicts.
	git am -3 "$file" || return
	# TODO: Replace with appropriate checks for this patch
	# (e.g. checkpatch.pl).
	true
}

validate_series () {
	# TODO: Replace with appropriate checks for the whole series
	# (e.g. quick build, coding style checks, etc.).
	true
}

# main -------------------------------------------------------------------------

if test "$GIT_SENDEMAIL_FILE_COUNTER" = 1
then
	remote=$(git config --default origin --get sendemail.validateRemote) &&
	ref=$(git config --default HEAD --get sendemail.validateRemoteRef) &&
	worktree=$(mktemp --tmpdir -d sendemail-validate.XXXXXXX) &&
	git worktree add -fd --checkout "$worktree" "refs/remotes/$remote/$ref" &&
	git config --replace-all sendemail.validateWorktree "$worktree"
else
	worktree=$(git config --get sendemail.validateWorktree)
fi || {
	echo "sendemail-validate: error: failed to prepare worktree" >&2
	exit 1
}

unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE
cd "$worktree" &&

if grep -q "^diff --git " "$1"
then
	validate_patch "$1"
else
	validate_cover_letter "$1"
fi &&

if test "$GIT_SENDEMAIL_FILE_COUNTER" = "$GIT_SENDEMAIL_FILE_TOTAL"
then
	git config --unset-all sendemail.validateWorktree &&
	trap 'git worktree remove -ff "$worktree"' EXIT &&
	validate_series
fi

<file path=".git/hooks/update.sample">
#!/bin/sh
#
# An example hook script to block unannotated tags from entering.
# Called by "git receive-pack" with arguments: refname sha1-old sha1-new
#
# To enable this hook, rename this file to "update".
#
# Config
# ------
# hooks.allowunannotated
#   This boolean sets whether unannotated tags will be allowed into the
#   repository.  By default they won't be.
# hooks.allowdeletetag
#   This boolean sets whether deleting tags will be allowed in the
#   repository.  By default they won't be.
# hooks.allowmodifytag
#   This boolean sets whether a tag may be modified after creation. By default
#   it won't be.
# hooks.allowdeletebranch
#   This boolean sets whether deleting branches will be allowed in the
#   repository.  By default they won't be.
# hooks.denycreatebranch
#   This boolean sets whether remotely creating branches will be denied
#   in the repository.  By default this is allowed.
#

# --- Command line
refname="$1"
oldrev="$2"
newrev="$3"

# --- Safety check
if [ -z "$GIT_DIR" ]; then
	echo "Don't run this script from the command line." >&2
	echo " (if you want, you could supply GIT_DIR then run" >&2
	echo "  $0 <ref> <oldrev> <newrev>)" >&2
	exit 1
fi

if [ -z "$refname" -o -z "$oldrev" -o -z "$newrev" ]; then
	echo "usage: $0 <ref> <oldrev> <newrev>" >&2
	exit 1
fi

# --- Config
allowunannotated=$(git config --type=bool hooks.allowunannotated)
allowdeletebranch=$(git config --type=bool hooks.allowdeletebranch)
denycreatebranch=$(git config --type=bool hooks.denycreatebranch)
allowdeletetag=$(git config --type=bool hooks.allowdeletetag)
allowmodifytag=$(git config --type=bool hooks.allowmodifytag)

# check for no description
projectdesc=$(sed -e '1q' "$GIT_DIR/description")
case "$projectdesc" in
"Unnamed repository"* | "")
	echo "*** Project description file hasn't been set" >&2
	exit 1
	;;
esac

# --- Check types
# if $newrev is 0000...0000, it's a commit to delete a ref.
zero=$(git hash-object --stdin </dev/null | tr '[0-9a-f]' '0')
if [ "$newrev" = "$zero" ]; then
	newrev_type=delete
else
	newrev_type=$(git cat-file -t $newrev)
fi

case "$refname","$newrev_type" in
	refs/tags/*,commit)
		# un-annotated tag
		short_refname=${refname##refs/tags/}
		if [ "$allowunannotated" != "true" ]; then
			echo "*** The un-annotated tag, $short_refname, is not allowed in this repository" >&2
			echo "*** Use 'git tag [ -a | -s ]' for tags you want to propagate." >&2
			exit 1
		fi
		;;
	refs/tags/*,delete)
		# delete tag
		if [ "$allowdeletetag" != "true" ]; then
			echo "*** Deleting a tag is not allowed in this repository" >&2
			exit 1
		fi
		;;
	refs/tags/*,tag)
		# annotated tag
		if [ "$allowmodifytag" != "true" ] && git rev-parse $refname > /dev/null 2>&1
		then
			echo "*** Tag '$refname' already exists." >&2
			echo "*** Modifying a tag is not allowed in this repository." >&2
			exit 1
		fi
		;;
	refs/heads/*,commit)
		# branch
		if [ "$oldrev" = "$zero" -a "$denycreatebranch" = "true" ]; then
			echo "*** Creating a branch is not allowed in this repository" >&2
			exit 1
		fi
		;;
	refs/heads/*,delete)
		# delete branch
		if [ "$allowdeletebranch" != "true" ]; then
			echo "*** Deleting a branch is not allowed in this repository" >&2
			exit 1
		fi
		;;
	refs/remotes/*,commit)
		# tracking branch
		;;
	refs/remotes/*,delete)
		# delete tracking branch
		if [ "$allowdeletebranch" != "true" ]; then
			echo "*** Deleting a tracking branch is not allowed in this repository" >&2
			exit 1
		fi
		;;
	*)
		# Anything else (is there anything else?)
		echo "*** Update hook: unknown type of update to ref $refname of type $newrev_type" >&2
		exit 1
		;;
esac

# --- Finished
exit 0
</file>

<!-- Hero Section -->
<section class="hero-section">
    <div class="hero-content">
        <h1 class="hero-title">How to Plan a Home Office That Actually Works in a UAE Home</h1>
        <div class="hero-meta">
            <span>2026-10-20</span> | <span>Author: <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">Theyyampattil GCC</a></span>
        </div>
        <p class="hero-intro">
            A good home office comes down to five choices: where the workspace sits, a desk sized to how you work, a chair you can sit in comfortably all day, storage that keeps paperwork and equipment out of sight, and lighting and power planned before the furniture arrives. Get these right and the space stays comfortable and productive, whether it is a spare room in a villa or a corner of an apartment.
        </p>
    </div>
</section>

<!-- Main Body Content -->
<main class="main-container">

    <!-- Row 1: Intro Text & Location -->
    <div class="grid-row">
        <div class="col-text">
            <p>
                This guide covers each choice in the order most homeowners meet them. It is written by Theyyampattil Furniture, which designs and manufactures furniture in-house for homes across Dubai, Sharjah, and Abu Dhabi, including made-to-measure study and office pieces.
            </p>
            <h2 class="section-title">Where to Put the Home Office: Spare Room, Corner, or Built-In Nook</h2>
            <p>
                The location decides the furniture. A full room allows a freestanding desk and storage wall, while a corner needs compact, well-planned pieces.
            </p>
            <h3 class="sub-title">Dedicated Room</h3>
            <p>
                A spare bedroom or study gives you the most freedom: a larger desk, bookcases, and a proper seating corner for reading or calls. Plan the layout so the desk faces the door or a window rather than a blank wall where possible.
            </p>
        </div>
        <div class="col-image">
            <img src="assets/images/home-page/3rd-section-desktop.avif" alt="Home Office Layout UAE" class="portrait-img" width="1607" height="1828" loading="lazy">
        </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Section Block: Rest of Location options -->
    <div class="section-block">
        <h3 class="sub-title">Living Room or Bedroom Corner</h3>
        <p>In apartments, a corner or alcove often has to do the job. Choose a compact desk and closed storage so the area can be visually tidied away at the end of the day.</p>
        
        <h3 class="sub-title">Built-In Study Nook</h3>
        <p>A made-to-measure nook with a desk, shelving, and cabinets built into one wall makes the most of awkward spaces and looks like part of the architecture rather than an add-on.</p>
    </div>

    <!-- Row 2: Desks with Alternate Image Alignment -->
    <div class="grid-row reverse">
        <div class="col-text">
            <h2 class="section-title">The Desk: Size, Shape, and Storage</h2>
            <p>
                Your desk should match your work, not just your room. Think about how many screens you use, whether you handle paper, and how much you need within arm's reach.
            </p>
            <h3 class="sub-title">Straight Desks</h3>
            <p>
                A straight desk suits most single-monitor setups and fits neatly against a wall or under a window. It is the simplest option for smaller rooms.
            </p>
            <h3 class="sub-title">L-Shaped and Corner Desks</h3>
            <p>
                An L-shaped desk gives separate zones for computer work and writing or paperwork. It works well in corners but needs more floor space, so check the clearance before choosing.
            </p>
        </div>
        <div class="col-image">
            <img src="assets/images/home-page/tv-wall.avif" alt="Custom Desk Setup UAE" class="portrait-img" width="1607" height="1828" loading="lazy">
        </div>
    </div>

    <div class="section-block">
        <h3 class="sub-title">Desks with Integrated Storage</h3>
        <p>Drawers, pedestal units, and cable-management openings keep the surface clear. Made-to-measure desks can place these exactly where you need them.</p>
    </div>

    <!-- Row 3: Chairs & Upholstery with Alternate Image Alignment -->
    <div class="grid-row">
        <div class="col-text">
            <h2 class="section-title">The Chair: Ergonomics First</h2>
            <p>
                You will spend more hours in the chair than at the desk itself, so its comfort and support matter more than its appearance.
            </p>
            <h3 class="sub-title">Height, Back Support, and Armrests</h3>
            <p>
                Look for adjustable seat height, proper lower-back support, and armrests that let your shoulders relax. Your feet should rest flat on the floor and your forearms should sit roughly level with the desk surface.
            </p>
            <h3 class="sub-title">Upholstery Choices</h3>
            <p>Choose upholstery for comfort over long hours and for how well it copes with the climate.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="col-image">
            <img src="assets/images/home-page/bed-room.avif" alt="Ergonomic Office Chair UAE" class="portrait-img" width="1607" height="1828" loading="lazy">
        </div>
    </div>

    <div class="section-block">
        <h4 class="sub-title-h4">Mesh</h4>
        <p>Mesh backs allow airflow and stay cooler, which many people appreciate in warm weather. Check that the support remains firm and comfortable.</p>
        
        <h4 class="sub-title-h4">Fabric</h4>
        <p>Fabric feels softer and warmer visually, and suits a home setting. Choose a tightly woven, durable fabric that keeps its shape.</p>
        
        <h4 class="sub-title-h4">Leather</h4>
        <p>Leather gives a polished look and is easy to wipe clean. Ask whether it is full-grain or a bonded alternative, as durability differs considerably.</p>
    </div>

    <!-- Section Block: Storage, Lighting, Materials -->
    <div class="section-block">
        <h2 class="section-title">Storage: Bookcases, Cabinets, and Filing</h2>
        <h3 class="sub-title">Open Shelving vs Closed Cabinets</h3>
        <p>Open shelves suit books and display items, while closed cabinets hide printers, files, and cables. A mix of both keeps the room attractive and functional.</p>
        
        <h3 class="sub-title">Cable and Equipment Management</h3>
        <p>Plan for chargers, routers, printers, and monitors from the start. Cutouts, cable channels, and a ventilated space for equipment prevent a tangle behind the desk and help devices run cooler.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="section-block">
        <h2 class="section-title">Lighting, Power, and Acoustics</h2>
        <h3 class="sub-title">Natural and Task Lighting</h3>
        <p>Position the desk so daylight falls from the side to reduce screen glare, and add a dedicated task light for evenings. Warm, dimmable ambient lighting makes the room more comfortable outside working hours.</p>

        <h3 class="sub-title">Power and Connectivity</h3>
        <p>Locate sockets and data points before the furniture is finalised so the desk and storage can be designed around them, rather than hiding cables afterward.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="section-block">
        <h2 class="section-title">Materials and Finishes for a Work Space</h2>
        <h3 class="sub-title">Desk Surfaces</h3>
        <p>A work surface should resist daily wear, spills, and heat from devices. Wood, quality veneer, and durable laminate-style finishes all work if well made, so ask how the edges and surface are protected.</p>

        <h3 class="sub-title">Climate Considerations</h3>
        <p>Keep wood furniture away from direct sun and air-conditioning vents, where concentrated airflow can dry and stress the material. Good joinery and well-chosen materials help the furniture stay stable in UAE conditions.</p>
    </div>

    <!-- Table Section -->
    <div class="section-block">
        <h2 class="section-title">Home Office Buying Checklist</h2>
        <div class="table-container">
            <table class="checklist-table">
                <thead>
                    <tr>
                        <th>Decision</th>
                        <th>What to Check</th>
                    </tr>
                </thead>

                        <td>Room, corner, or built-in nook that suits how you work</td>
                    </tr>

                        <td>Size, shape, and storage matched to your equipment</td>
                    </tr>

                        <td>Mix of open shelving and closed cabinets</td>

                        <td>Sockets planned first; cable management built in</td>

                    </tr>
                </tbody>
            </table>
        </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Hero Section -->
    <header class="hero-section">
        <div class="hero-content">
            <h1 class="hero-title">How to Design a Headboard Wall That Makes Your Bedroom Feel Like a Suite</h1>
            <div class="hero-meta">
                Published on <?php echo date('F j, Y'); ?> | By <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">Theyyampattil GCC</a>
            </div>
        </div>
    </header>

    <!-- Main Body Content -->
    <main class="content-container">
        
        <!-- Section: Intro -->
        <section class="section-block">
            <p>A luxury bed panel is a made-to-measure headboard wall that frames the bed, adds texture and softness, and anchors the whole bedroom design. The best ones combine the right style (upholstered, wood, or mixed), proportions suited to the bed and the ceiling height, integrated lighting and bedside storage, and materials that handle the UAE climate. Done well, it makes a bedroom feel finished and hotel-like.</p>
            <p>This guide walks through each decision in the order most homeowners meet them. It is written by Theyyampattil Furniture, which designs and manufactures bed panels and bedroom joinery in-house for villas and apartments across Dubai, Sharjah, and Abu Dhabi.</p>
        </section>

        <!-- Section: What Is a Bed Panel -->
        <section class="section-block">
            <h2>What Is a Bed Panel and Why It Matters</h2>
            <h3>More Than a Headboard</h3>
            <p>A standard headboard is attached to the bed. A bed panel is a wall treatment behind it, designed to the width and height of the wall, and it often carries lighting, side units, and decorative detail. It turns the headboard wall into the focal point of the room.</p>
            <h3>Where It Fits in the Bedroom Layout</h3>
            <p>The bed panel anchors the layout: the wardrobes, dressing area, and any TV wall are easier to plan once the headboard wall is defined. Decide it early in the design.</p>
        </section>

        <!-- Section: Bed Panel Styles (Contains Image 1) -->
        <section class="section-block">
            <div class="split-row">
                <div class="split-image-wrapper">
                    <!-- Image 1: Size 1607 x 1828 px placeholder -->
                    <img src="assets/images/home-page/bed-room.avif" alt="Luxury Upholstered Bed Panel" class="split-image" width="1607" height="1828" loading="lazy">
                </div>
                <div class="split-text">
                    <h2>Bed Panel Styles: Upholstered, Wood, and Mixed</h2>
                    <h3>Upholstered Panels</h3>
                    <p>Upholstered panels bring softness and warmth and suit a calm, hotel-style look. The detailing sets the character.</p>
                    <h4>Channel and Vertical Padding</h4>
                    <p>Clean vertical lines add height and a tailored feel, and work well in contemporary rooms.</p>
                    <h4>Tufted Detailing</h4>
                    <p>Button or diamond tufting adds a more classic, decorative finish that suits traditional and modern-classic interiors.</p>
                    <h4>Flat or Framed Fabric Panels</h4>
                    <p>Smooth fabric panels set within slim frames or mouldings create a quiet, refined look with minimal pattern.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
            
            <h3>Wood and Fluted Panels</h3>
            <p>Wood and fluted panels add warmth and texture, and pair naturally with warm, natural palettes and Italian-inspired interiors. They are also easy to wipe down.</p>
            
            <h3>Mixed-Material Panels</h3>
            <p>Combining fabric, wood, and metal or stone-look accents gives the headboard wall depth and a more custom, high-end appearance. Keep the proportions and detailing precise so it stays elegant rather than busy.</p>
        </section>

        <!-- Section: Sizing & Proportions + Integrated Lighting (Contains Image 2) -->
        <section class="section-block">
            <div class="split-row reverse">
                <div class="split-image-wrapper">
                    <!-- Image 2: Size 1607 x 1828 px placeholder -->
                    <img src="assets/images/bed/bed-2.jpeg" alt="Bed Panel Sizing and Integrated Lighting" class="split-image" width="1607" height="1828" loading="lazy">
                </div>
                <div class="split-text">
                    <h2>Sizing and Proportions: Width, Height, and Wall Coverage</h2>
                    <h3>Width</h3>
                    <p>Many designers make the panel wider than the bed so it can hold bedside tables or wall-mounted units and frame the bed properly. The right width depends on your wall and the furniture you want on either side.</p>
                    <h3>Height and Ceiling</h3>
                    <p>A taller panel makes the room feel grander, especially with high ceilings, while a lower one feels cosier. Some designs run floor to ceiling for a dramatic effect. Match the height to the room's proportions.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </section>

        <!-- Section: Integrated Lighting, Bedside Units, and Power -->
        <section class="section-block">
            <h2>Integrated Lighting, Bedside Units, and Power</h2>
            <h3>Lighting</h3>
            <p>Warm LED strips behind or around the panel, wall-mounted reading lights, and dimmable ambient lighting set a relaxing atmosphere. Plan the cabling and drivers at design stage so everything is concealed.</p>
            <h3>Bedside Units and Power</h3>
            <p>Floating bedside units, built-in shelves, and concealed sockets and USB points keep the area tidy and practical. Decide socket positions before the panel is made.</p>
        </section>

        <!-- Section: Materials & Room Matching (Contains Image 3) -->
        <section class="section-block">
            <div class="split-row">
                <div class="split-image-wrapper">
                    <!-- Image 3: Size 1607 x 1828 px placeholder -->
                    <img src="assets/images/bed/bed-5.jpeg" alt="Materials and Room Matching for Bed Panels" class="split-image" width="1607" height="1828" loading="lazy">
                </div>
                <div class="split-text">
                    <h2>Materials and Finishes for UAE Bedrooms</h2>
                    <h3>Fabrics and Cleaning</h3>
                    <p>Choose tightly woven, durable upholstery that is comfortable to touch and easy to maintain. Ask how the fabric can be cleaned and how it holds up to everyday contact with hair and skin.</p>
                    <h3>Wood and Climate</h3>
                    <p>Keep wood panels away from direct sun and strong air-conditioning airflow where possible, and ask the maker how the materials and joinery are prepared for Gulf humidity and dry indoor air.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </section>

        <!-- Section: Matching Room & TV Walls -->
        <section class="section-block">
            <h2>Matching the Bed Panel to the Rest of the Room</h2>
            <h3>Wardrobes and Dressing Areas</h3>
            <p>Use the same wood tones, fabrics, and handle details across the bed panel, wardrobes, and dressing unit so the bedroom reads as one design.</p>
            <h3>TV Walls in Bedrooms</h3>
            <p>If the bedroom has a TV, plan it opposite the bed with matching paneling so both walls feel connected rather than competing.</p>
        </section>

        <!-- Section: Buying Checklist -->
        <section class="section-block">
            <h2>Bed Panel Buying Checklist</h2>
            <div class="table-responsive">
                <table class="checklist-table">
                    <thead>
                        <tr>
                            <th>Decision</th>
                            <th>What to Check</th>
                        </tr>
                    </thead>
                    <tbody>
                        <tr>
                            <td><strong>Style</strong></td>
                            <td>Upholstered, wood, or mixed to suit the room</td>
                        </tr>
                        <tr>
                            <td><strong>Width and height</strong></td>
                            <td>Proportioned to the bed, wall, and ceiling</td>
                        </tr>
                        <tr>
                            <td><strong>Lighting</strong></td>
                            <td>Integrated, dimmable, and fully concealed</td>
                        </tr>

    <!-- Intro Section -->
    <div class="full-text-section">
        <p>Furnishing a Dubai villa with luxury home furniture works best when each room is planned around how it is used, then tied together by a consistent palette, material family, and design language. Start with the rooms that define the home, such as the <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/product/luxury-living-room-furniture-uae/">living area</a>, master bedroom, and <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/product/walk-in-closets-wardrobes-uae/">walk-in closet</a>, choose made-to-measure pieces where fit matters, and keep finishes cohesive from room to room.</p>
        <p>A villa has many rooms to furnish, and buying piece by piece often leads to a home that feels disconnected. Theyyampattil Furniture designs and manufactures furniture in-house for villas across Dubai, Sharjah, and Abu Dhabi. Here is a room-by-room guide to furnishing yours with a clear, cohesive plan.</p>

    <!-- Section: Whole-Home Plan -->
    <div class="full-text-section">
        <h2>Start With a Whole-Home Plan</h2>
        <h3>Choose One Design Language</h3>
        <p>Decide on an overall direction, such as warm minimalism, Italian-inspired, or modern classic, before choosing individual pieces. This keeps every room feeling part of the same home.</p>
        <h3>Limit Your Palette and Materials</h3>
        <p>Pick a core set of wood tones, fabric textures, and metal or stone accents, and repeat them throughout the villa. Repetition creates cohesion without making rooms identical.</p>
        <h3>Plan Built-Ins Before Loose Furniture</h3>
        <p>Wall panels, TV units, closets, and kitchens are fixed elements, so design them first. Loose furniture can then be chosen to complement them.</p>
    </div>

            <div class="faq-answer">

        </div>

            <div class="faq-answer">

        <div class="faq-item">

<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
    var popup = document.getElementById('homePromoPopup');
    if (!popup) return;

    // Show popup immediately
    popup.style.display = 'flex'; // Force display flex
    // Small delay to ensure CSS transition triggers
    setTimeout(function() {
        popup.classList.add('active');
        popup.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'false');
        document.body.classList.add('home-popup-open');
    }, 50);

    var closeBtn = popup.querySelector('.home-popup-close');

    function closePopup() {
        popup.classList.remove('active');
        popup.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
        document.body.classList.remove('home-popup-open');
        // Optional: Hide display after transition finishes so it doesn't block clicks
        setTimeout(function() {
            popup.style.display = 'none';
        }, 350);
    }

    if (closeBtn) {
        closeBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
            e.stopPropagation();
            closePopup();
        });
    }

    popup.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target === popup) {
            closePopup();
        }
    });

    document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Escape' && popup.classList.contains('active')) {
            closePopup();
        }
    });
});
</script>

    <div class="intro-text">
        <p>In 2026, Dubai homeowners are moving toward warm minimalism, natural materials, custom wall paneling, and multi-functional furniture that balances luxury with everyday livability. The shift is away from cold, ultra-glossy maximalism and toward interiors that feel curated, textural, and personal while still reflecting the premium standards UAE homes are known for.</p>
        <p>As Theyyampattil Furniture, working across Dubai, Sharjah, and Abu Dhabi villas and apartments, we see these shifts firsthand in what homeowners and interior designers are actually requesting. Here are the trends defining UAE interiors this year.</p>
    </div>

    <!-- Trend 1 with Image 1 (Left Image, Right Text) -->

        </div>
        <div class="col-text">
            <h2>1. Warm Minimalism Replaces Cold Luxury</h2>
            <h3>What's Changing</h3>
            <p>The high-gloss, all-white, ultra-reflective look that dominated luxury interiors for years is softening. Homeowners are now choosing warm neutral palettes - taupe, sand, soft bronze paired with matte and textured finishes instead of high-shine surfaces.</p>
            <h3>Where You'll See It</h3>
            <p>Living rooms and bedrooms with fewer, more intentional statement pieces rather than densely furnished, showroom-style layouts.</p>
        </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Trend 2 (Text Only) -->
    <div class="section-block">
        <h2>2. Natural and Textured Materials Take Priority</h2>
        <h3>What's Changing</h3>
        <p>Solid wood, natural stone-look finishes, boucle and linen upholstery, and hand-finished details are replacing uniform, mass-produced surfaces. Texture is doing the work that heavy ornamentation used to do.</p>
        <h3>Where You'll See It</h3>
        <p>Dining tables, TV wall units, and headboards featuring natural wood grain and tactile fabric finishes rather than flat lacquer or high-gloss panels.</p>
    </div>

    <!-- Trend 3 with Image 2 (Right Image, Left Text) -->

        <div class="col-image">

        </div>
        <div class="col-text">
            <h2>3. Custom Wall Panels and Wood Accent Walls</h2>
            <h3>What's Changing</h3>
            <p>Wall panels have moved from a niche feature to a defining element of modern UAE interiors used to add texture, zone open-plan spaces, and create a backdrop for TV units and headboards without relying on paint or wallpaper alone.</p>
            <h3>Where You'll See It</h3>
            <p>Feature walls behind beds, living room TV units, and entryways, often combining wood paneling with integrated lighting. This is one of the most requested solutions in Theyyampattil Furniture's wall panel projects across Dubai homes.</p>
        </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Trend 4 (Text Only) -->
    <div class="section-block">
        <h2>4. Walk-In Closets as a Standard Expectation, Not a Luxury Add-On</h2>
        <h3>What's Changing</h3>
        <p>What was once reserved for high-end villas is now a standard request across both villa and larger apartment projects a dedicated, well-organized walk-in closet with custom shelving, lighting, and display sections.</p>
        <h3>Where You'll See It</h3>
        <p>Master bedrooms in new villa developments and larger apartment renovations across Dubai and Abu Dhabi a category where Theyyampattil Furniture has built deep expertise through custom walk-in closet design and installation.</p>
    </div>

    <!-- Trend 5 with Image 3 (Left Image, Right Text) -->

        <div class="col-image">
            <img src="assets/images/home-page/dressing-unit.avif" alt="Multi-Functional Furniture">
        </div>
        <div class="col-text">
            <h2>5. Multi-Functional Furniture for Flexible Living</h2>
            <h3>What's Changing</h3>
            <p>As home offices, guest arrangements, and multi-generational living become more common, furniture is being designed to do more than one job - storage beds, extendable dining tables, and modular seating that reconfigures easily.</p>
            <h3>Where You'll See It</h3>
            <p>Apartment living rooms and smaller villa guest rooms where flexibility matters as much as style.</p>
        </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Trend 6 (Text Only) -->
    <div class="section-block">
        <h2>6. Statement Lighting as a Design Anchor</h2>
        <h3>What's Changing</h3>
        <p>Lighting is being treated as a design centerpiece rather than a functional afterthought - sculptural pendant lights, integrated LED detailing in wall panels and ceilings, and warm, layered lighting schemes replacing single overhead fixtures.</p>
        <h3>Where You'll See It</h3>
        <p>Dining areas, majlis spaces, and feature walls where lighting highlights texture and architecture.</p>

            <h3>Where You'll See It</h3>
            <p>Requests for solid wood over veneer, UV-resistant fabrics, and finishes specifically chosen for longevity in Gulf conditions a priority Theyyampattil Furniture builds into every in-house manufactured piece.</p>

            const isActive = faqItem.classList.contains('active');
            
            document.querySelectorAll('.faq-item').forEach(item => {
                item.classList.remove('active');
            });

            if (!isActive) {
                faqItem.classList.add('active');
            }
        });
    });

            <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">Home</a>

            <span class="current">Custom Luxury Furniture in Sharjah: A Complete Buyer's Guide</span>
        </nav>
        <h1>Custom Luxury Furniture in Sharjah: A Complete Buyer's Guide</h1>
    </div>
</section>

<!-- Main Content Section -->
<section class="content-section">
    <div class="container">
        
        <p class="intro-text">
            Sharjah's villas, apartments, and commercial spaces call for furniture that's built to measure rather than picked off a showroom floor. With a growing base of homeowners and businesses across the emirate investing in bespoke interiors, custom luxury furniture has become the standard for anyone who wants a space that actually reflects its architecture not just fills it.
        </p>

        <p>
            This guide covers what custom furniture in Sharjah involves, which materials separate genuine bespoke work from mass production, realistic manufacturing timelines, and what to look for in a workshop before you commit using the process followed by Theyyampattil Furniture, a Sharjah-based custom furniture workshop, as a reference point throughout.
        </p>

        <!-- Section 1 with Integrated Image 1 -->
        <h2>What Makes Furniture "Custom" in Sharjah?</h2>
        <div class="grid-2">
            <div>
                <p>Custom furniture in Sharjah means every piece is designed around one specific room rather than pulled from a standard product line. A workshop building bespoke furniture starts from your measurements and material choices, not from a template that gets slightly adjusted.</p>
                <p>The scale of the project changes what "custom" actually needs to solve:</p>
                <ul>
                    <li>In a large villa, the challenge is usually covering a lot of ground consistently - seating, dining, and wall treatments that all read as one design across several oversized rooms.</li>
                    <li>In an apartment or penthouse, the priority flips to efficiency - getting real storage and a livable layout out of a smaller, often irregular floor plan.</li>
                    <li>In a commercial space, furniture needs to hold up to daily use while still projecting the right image to clients and staff.</li>
                    <li>In a hotel or resort, pieces need to survive constant turnover and heavy use without looking worn down within a year or two.</li>
                </ul>
            </div>
            <div class="img-container">
                <img src="assets/images/gallery/part-0.jpg" alt="Custom Villa Interior Design in Sharjah" loading="lazy">
            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- Section 2 with Integrated Image 2 -->
        <h2>What Materials Should You Expect in Genuine Bespoke Furniture?</h2>
        <div class="grid-2">
            <div class="img-container">
                <img src="assets/images/gallery/welcome-unit.JPEG" alt="Bespoke High End Materials and Wood Finishes" loading="lazy">
            </div>
            <div>
                <p>The materials list is the fastest way to tell a genuine custom workshop from one that's just modifying stock pieces. Ask what a supplier actually builds with - vague answers like "premium wood" are a red flag. Workshops doing real bespoke work in Sharjah generally specify:</p>
                <ul>
                    <li>Laminated sheeting rated for structural use, not just decorative surfaces</li>
                    <li>Engineered wood carrying a European certification, chosen specifically because it holds up better in the region's heat and humidity than untreated timber</li>
                    <li>Foam density high enough that cushions don't flatten out within a year or two of daily use</li>
                    <li>Fabric and leather sourced from European and Italian suppliers rather than generic upholstery rolls</li>
                    <li>Marble and stone imported for tabletops and other surfaces meant to be the room's focal point</li>
                </ul>
                <p>If a quote is notably cheaper than competitors, one of these five is almost always where the corner got cut.</p>
            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- Section 3: Categories -->
        <h2>Custom Furniture Categories Common in Sharjah Homes</h2>
        <div class="categories-grid">
            <div class="category-card">
                <h3>Walk-in Closets</h3>
                <p>Full wardrobe systems built into the room's actual footprint, so shelving, hanging space, and drawers use every inch rather than fighting an awkward layout.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="category-card">
                <h3>Luxury Kitchens</h3>
                <p>Cabinetry and dining furniture produced as a matched set with solid wood or marble worktops, the dining table designed to sit alongside the same finish.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="category-card">
                <h3>TV Wall Units</h3>
                <p>Media walls that double as storage, hiding cables and electronics behind the same panel finish used elsewhere in the room.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="category-card">
                <h3>Bedroom Furniture</h3>
                <p>King and queen bed frames with upholstered headboards, paired with bedside tables built to the same proportions and finish.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="category-card">
                <h3>Wall Panels</h3>
                <p>Acoustic and decorative panelling in hardwood, leather, or mixed finishes, used to tie a room's walls into its overall design theme.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="category-card">
                <h3>Dressing Areas</h3>
                <p>A dedicated vanity and dressing table setup with built-in lighting and storage worked into the design from the start, rather than added afterward.</p>
            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- Section 4 with Integrated Image 3 -->
        <h2>How Long Does Custom Furniture Take to Manufacture in Sharjah?</h2>
        <div class="grid-2">
            <div>
                <p>Expect roughly five to seven weeks between confirming your design and having it delivered. The exact number moves based on how many pieces are involved and how intricate the joinery, finishes, or upholstery work is a single dressing table can be finished well before a full villa order with paneling, seating, and built-in storage all going through production together.</p>
                <p>This is longer than off-the-shelf furniture delivery for a reason: each piece goes through consultation, concept design, material sourcing, and manufacturing before it ever reaches installation.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="img-container">
                <img src="assets/images/closets/closet-3.jpeg" alt="Furniture Manufacturing Workshop" loading="lazy">
            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- Section 5: Process -->
        <h2>The Custom Furniture Process, Step by Step</h2>
        <p>Theyyampattil Furniture breaks the work into six stages, from first meeting to final walkthrough:</p>
        
        <div class="process-list">
            <div class="process-step">
                <strong>1. Consultation</strong> - a design specialist reviews your space, priorities, and budget to scope the project
            </div>
            <div class="process-step">
                <strong>2. Concept</strong> - initial design direction and layout planning
            </div>
            <div class="process-step">
                <strong>3. Materials</strong> - selecting wood types, fabrics, leather, and stone finishes
            </div>
            <div class="process-step">
                <strong>4. Manufacturing</strong> - building each piece to exact specifications
            </div>
            <div class="process-step">
                <strong>5. Installation</strong> - professional delivery and on-site fitting
            </div>
            <div class="process-step">
                <strong>6. After Sales</strong> - support once the furniture is installed
            </div>
        </div>
        
        <p>Many established workshops also offer on-site interior measurement consultations and 3D visualization before production starts, so you can see how a design will look before committing.</p>

        <!-- Section 6 with Integrated Image 4 -->
        <h2>Choosing a Custom Furniture Workshop in Sharjah</h2>
        <div class="grid-2">
            <div class="img-container">
                <img src="assets/images/bed/bed-7.jpeg" alt="Luxury Showroom in Sharjah" loading="lazy">
            </div>
            <div>
                <p>A few signals separate a genuine bespoke workshop from a reseller offering "customization" on stock items:</p>
                <ul>
                    <li>A real workshop or factory location you can visit, not just a showroom</li>
                    <li>Named material specifications for every piece, not vague terms like "premium"</li>
                    <li>On-site measurement and 3D visualization before production</li>
                    <li>A defined, staged process from consultation through after-sales support</li>
                    <li>Verified client reviews referencing specific projects or staff by name</li>
                </ul>
                <p>Theyyampattil Furniture, for example, operates its Sharjah showroom and factory at Warehouses Land, serving clients across Sharjah, Dubai, and Abu Dhabi. Their process runs through the six stages outlined above, with on-site measurement consultations and 3D visualization available before manufacturing begins.</p>
            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- FAQ Section -->
        <div class="faq-section">
            <h2>Frequently Asked Questions About Custom Furniture in Sharjah</h2>
            
            <div class="faq-item">
                <button class="faq-question">How much does custom furniture cost in Sharjah?</button>
                <div class="faq-answer">
                    <p>Pricing depends on the piece, material, and finish chosen, with villa-scale packages costing more than single items. Most workshops provide a detailed quote after the initial consultation once your requirements are confirmed.</p>
                </div>
            </div>

            <div class="faq-item">
                <button class="faq-question">What is the difference between custom furniture and ready-made furniture?</button>
                <div class="faq-answer">
                    <p>Ready-made furniture comes in fixed sizes and finishes, while custom furniture is built to your room's exact measurements and your choice of materials. This makes custom furniture better suited to non-standard layouts like large villas or compact apartments.</p>
                </div>
            </div>

            <div class="faq-item">
                <button class="faq-question">Can I see a 3D design before my furniture is manufactured?</button>
                <div class="faq-answer">
                    <p>Yes. Most Sharjah-based custom furniture workshops provide a 3D visualization of the design so you can review layout, proportions, and finishes before production begins.</p>
                </div>
            </div>

            <div class="faq-item">
                <button class="faq-question">Do I need to visit the showroom, or can everything be done remotely?</button>
                <div class="faq-answer">
                    <p>An initial site visit or measurement consultation is usually required for accuracy, but material selection and design approval can often be completed remotely once measurements are confirmed.</p>
                </div>
            </div>

            <div class="faq-item">
                <button class="faq-question">Is custom furniture in Sharjah suitable for small apartments, or only large villas?</button>
                <div class="faq-answer">
                    <p>Both. Custom furniture is often more practical for small apartments, since space-saving and modular designs can be built to fit exact room dimensions that standard furniture can't.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- Final Thoughts -->
        <div class="final-thoughts">
            <h3>Final Thoughts</h3>
            <p>Custom furniture in Sharjah is a longer commitment than buying off the shelf - both in decision-making and production time but it's the only route to furniture that's actually built for your space. Before committing to a workshop, ask for the specific materials they use, a realistic manufacturing timeline, and whether on-site measurement is included. Those answers will tell you whether you're getting genuine bespoke work or a resized standard product.</p>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 0; font-weight: 600; color: #ffffff;">Ready to design your space? Visit the Sharjah showroom at Warehouses Land, or call 06 767 6297 to book a free consultation.</p>
        </div>

    </div>
</section>

<script>
    // FAQ Accordion Toggle Script
    document.querySelectorAll('.faq-question').forEach(button => {
        button.addEventListener('click', () => {
            const faqItem = button.parentElement;
            
            // Close other open FAQs
            document.querySelectorAll('.faq-item').forEach(item => {
                if (item !== faqItem) {
                    item.classList.remove('active');
                }
            });

            // Toggle current FAQ
            faqItem.classList.toggle('active');
        });
    });
</script>

<!-- Hero Section -->
<section class="hero-section">
    <div class="hero-content">
        <h1 class="hero-title">How to Choose a Custom Furniture Maker in Dubai: 7 Questions to Ask</h1>
        <div class="hero-meta">
            September 25, 2026 | By <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">Theyyampattil GCC</a>
        </div>
    </div>
</section>

<!-- Page Content -->
<main class="page-container">

    <div class="intro-text">
        <p>The right custom furniture maker in Dubai should be judged on in-house manufacturing capability, material transparency, project timelines, after-sales support, and a physical showroom you can visit - not just on portfolio photos. Asking the right questions upfront prevents the two most common problems homeowners face: mismatched expectations on timelines, and furniture quality that doesn't match the showroom sample.</p>
        <p>With dozens of furniture brands operating across Dubai, Sharjah, and Abu Dhabi, it's easy to pick based on price or Instagram photos alone. Here are the seven questions worth asking before you commit to any custom furniture maker and why each one matters.</p>
    </div>

    <!-- Row 1: Image Left, Text Right -->
    <div class="content-row">
        <div class="col-image">
            <img src="assets/images/home-page/tv-wall.avif" alt="In-House Custom Furniture Manufacturing Workshop">
        </div>
        <div class="col-text">
            <h2>1. Do You Manufacture In-House or Outsource Production?</h2>
            <h3>Why This Question Matters</h3>
            <p>Many furniture "brands" in the UAE are actually resellers who outsource production to third-party workshops, which means less control over quality, longer communication chains, and inconsistent finishing. A maker with in-house manufacturing facilities can control quality at every stage and adjust designs quickly without delays caused by external vendors.</p>
            <p><strong>What to listen for:</strong> A specific answer naming their own factory or production facility not a vague "we work with trusted partners."</p>
        </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Row 2: Text Left, Image Right (Reversed) -->
    <div class="content-row reverse">
        <div class="col-image">
            <img src="assets/images/home-page/bed-room.avif" alt="Physical Custom Furniture Material Samples">
        </div>
        <div class="col-text">
            <h2>2. Can I See and Touch Material Samples Before Production Starts?</h2>
            <h3>Why This Question Matters</h3>
            <p>Photos and renders can be misleading wood grain, leather texture, and fabric color all look different in person versus on a screen. A reliable furniture maker should provide physical material samples during the design phase so you know exactly what you're approving before manufacturing begins.</p>
            <p><strong>What to listen for:</strong> Willingness to bring or show samples at a showroom visit, not just digital mood boards.</p>
        </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Text Block: Question 3 -->
    <div class="text-block">
        <h2>3. What Is the Realistic Timeline From Design Approval to Installation?</h2>
        <h3>Why This Question Matters</h3>
        <p>Custom furniture timelines vary significantly depending on complexity, material availability, and current workshop capacity. A trustworthy maker will give you a realistic range (typically several weeks) rather than an overly optimistic promise designed to win the sale.</p>
        <p><strong>What to listen for:</strong> A clear breakdown of phases - design sign-off, manufacturing, quality check, delivery, and installation rather than a single vague number.</p>
    </div>

    <!-- Row 3: Image Left, Text Right -->
    <div class="content-row">
        <div class="col-image">
            <img src="assets/images/home-page/wall-panel.avif" alt="Custom Furniture Installation in Dubai">
        </div>
        <div class="col-text">
            <h2>4. Is Installation Included, and Who Handles It?</h2>
            <h3>Why This Question Matters</h3>
            <p>Custom furniture, especially built-ins like wardrobes, TV units, and wall panels, needs to be installed precisely to match architectural measurements. If installation is outsourced to a separate team unfamiliar with the original design intent, fit and finish can suffer.</p>
            <p><strong>What to listen for:</strong> Confirmation that the same company handling design and manufacturing also manages installation, ensuring consistency from concept to completion.</p>
        </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Text Block: Question 5 -->
    <div class="text-block">
        <h2>5. What Happens if Something Needs Adjustment After Installation?</h2>
        <h3>Why This Question Matters</h3>
        <p>Even with precise measurements, minor adjustments (a door alignment, a drawer glide, a panel gap) sometimes come up after installation. A furniture maker's after-sales policy tells you a lot about how seriously they stand behind their work.</p>
        <p><strong>What to listen for:</strong> A clear warranty or after-sales support policy, not just a one-time sale-and-done relationship.</p>
    </div>

    <!-- Row 4: Text Left, Image Right (Reversed) -->
    <div class="content-row reverse">
        <div class="col-image">
            <img src="assets/images/home-page/kitchen.avif" alt="Luxury Custom Furniture Showroom">
        </div>
        <div class="col-text">
            <h2>6. Can I Visit a Showroom to See Finished Work in Person?</h2>
            <h3>Why This Question Matters</h3>
            <p>A physical showroom lets you inspect real finished pieces - joinery quality, hardware, finishing consistency - rather than relying on curated photography. Brands confident in their craftsmanship are typically happy to host in-person visits.</p>
            <p><strong>What to listen for:</strong> Multiple showroom locations (a sign of an established, scaled operation) and an open invitation to visit before you commit.</p>
        </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Text Block: Question 7 -->
    <div class="text-block">
        <h2>7. How Do You Handle Design Changes Mid-Project?</h2>
        <h3>Why This Question Matters</h3>
        <p>Homeowners sometimes want to adjust a detail after seeing initial samples or mock-ups. Understanding how flexible (or rigid) a company is about changes mid-process and whether that affects the timeline helps set realistic expectations from day one.</p>
        <p><strong>What to listen for:</strong> A defined change-request process rather than "that's not really possible once we start."</p>
    </div>

    <!-- Quick Checklist Table -->
    <div class="text-block">
        <h2>Quick Checklist Before You Sign</h2>
        <div class="table-responsive">
            <table class="custom-table">
                <thead>
                    <tr>
                        <th>Question</th>
                        <th>Green Flag Answer</th>
                    </tr>
                </thead>
                <tbody>
                    <tr>
                        <td>In-house or outsourced?</td>
                        <td>Owns and names their own facility</td>
                    </tr>
                    <tr>
                        <td>Material samples?</td>
                        <td>Offers physical samples pre-production</td>
                    </tr>
                    <tr>
                        <td>Timeline?</td>
                        <td>Gives phase-by-phase breakdown</td>
                    </tr>
                    <tr>
                        <td>Installation?</td>
                        <td>Same team, end-to-end</td>
                    </tr>
                    <tr>
                        <td>After-sales support?</td>
                        <td>Clear warranty/adjustment policy</td>
                    </tr>
                    <tr>
                        <td>Showroom visit?</td>
                        <td>Multiple locations, open invitation</td>
                    </tr>
                    <tr>
                        <td>Mid-project changes?</td>
                        <td>Defined process, transparent about impact</td>
                    </tr>
                </tbody>
            </table>
        </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Theyyampattil Section -->

Every project starts with an in-person consultation and material sign-off, and our three showrooms are open for homeowners and interior designers to inspect finished craftsmanship before committing to a project.</p>

    <!-- Interactive FAQ Section -->
    <div class="faq-section">
        <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
        
        <div class="faq-item">
            <button class="faq-question">How do I verify if a furniture company actually manufactures in-house?</button>
            <div class="faq-answer">
                <p>Ask to visit their production facility, or check if they can name and show their own factory rather than referring vaguely to manufacturing partners. Established brands are usually transparent about this.</p>
            </div>
        </div>

        <div class="faq-item">
            <button class="faq-question">What's a reasonable timeline for custom furniture in Dubai?</button>
            <div class="faq-answer">
                <p>Timelines vary by project complexity, but most custom furniture projects - from design sign-off to installation - take several weeks. Always ask for a phase-by-phase breakdown rather than a single estimate.</p>
            </div>
        </div>

        <div class="faq-item">
            <button class="faq-question">Should I choose a furniture maker with multiple showrooms?</button>
            <div class="faq-answer">
                <p>Multiple showrooms often indicate an established, scaled operation with consistent production standards, but the most important factor is still visiting in person to assess craftsmanship quality directly.</p>
            </div>
        </div>

        <div class="faq-item">
            <button class="faq-question">What questions should I avoid skipping when hiring a custom furniture maker?</button>

<script>
    // FAQ Accordion Interaction
    document.querySelectorAll('.faq-question').forEach(button => {
        button.addEventListener('click', () => {
            const faqItem = button.parentElement;
            const isActive = faqItem.classList.contains('active');
            
            // Close all open FAQs
            document.querySelectorAll('.faq-item').forEach(item => {
                item.classList.remove('active');
            });

            // Toggle current FAQ
            if (!isActive) {
                faqItem.classList.add('active');
            }
        });
    });
</script>

            <h1>Italian-Inspired Luxury Furniture in Dubai: Design Features, Materials &amp; Styles</h1>
            <div class="hero-meta">
                <span>By <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">Theyyampattil GCC</a></span>
                <span class="separator">|</span>
                <span>October 8, 2026</span>
            </div>
