        <h2>How to Prepare for Your Showroom Visit</h2>
        <div class="direct-answer">
            <strong>Quick Answer:</strong> Bring floor measurements, room photos, and budget targets so our design consultants can provide accurate technical feedback immediately.
        </div>
        <p>A little preparation goes a long way toward making your showroom visit productive. Before you come in, it helps to:</p>
        <ul>
            <li>Take photos and measurements of your space — even rough dimensions of the room, doorways, and existing furniture help our designers give accurate advice</li>
            <li>Bring inspiration images — screenshots of styles, colors, or layouts you like (Pinterest boards work fine)</li>
            <li>Know your rough budget — this helps our team recommend materials and configurations that fit, rather than showing you everything</li>
            <li>Think about function first — how many people need to sit at the dining table, how much storage you need, whether the piece needs to suit a rental or a long-term home</li>
            <li>Ask about materials and care — solid hardwood, marble, and leather each have different maintenance needs, so it's worth asking upfront</li>
        </ul>

<!-- Interactive Script for FAQ Accordion -->
<script>
    function toggleFaq(button) {
        const item = button.parentElement;
        const isActive = item.classList.contains('active');
        
        // Close all active items
        document.querySelectorAll('.faq-item').forEach(el => {
            el.classList.remove('active');
            el.querySelector('.faq-body').style.maxHeight = null;
        });

        // Toggle clicked item
        if (!isActive) {
            item.classList.add('active');
            const body = item.querySelector('.faq-body');
            body.style.maxHeight = body.scrollHeight + 30 + "px";
        }
    }
</script>

        <p>In Dubai's most discerning homes, the wardrobe is no longer a room you store clothes in—it is a room you get dressed in. And that distinction transforms how the entire space is experienced.</p>
        <p>If you are searching for a custom walk-in closet in Dubai, you already understand that a standard fitted wardrobe from a catalogue cannot do justice to a curated wardrobe, a well-considered space, or a home that has been designed with intention. This guide will walk you through everything you need to know - from design options and materials to timelines, and what to look for in a luxury closet designer in the UAE.</p>

    <section class="section">
        <h2>Walk-In Closet vs Fitted Wardrobe vs Dressing Room What Is Right for You?</h2>
        <p>Before commissioning any bespoke storage solution, it helps to understand the three categories and which one genuinely fits your space and lifestyle.</p>
        
        <div class="split-layout">
            <div class="content-column">
                <h3>Fitted Wardrobe</h3>
                <p>A fitted wardrobe is built directly into a wall or alcove, floor-to-ceiling, maximising every centimetre of a bedroom. It is the most space-efficient option and works well in apartments or bedrooms without a dedicated dressing area.</p>
                <p>At Theyyampattil, we design fitted wardrobes with custom internal configurations - hanging rails at different heights, pull-out shoe racks, velvet-lined drawers, and integrated LED lighting so that even a compact wardrobe feels like a premium experience.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="image-column">
                <img src="assets/images/closets/closet-1.jpeg" alt="Bespoke luxury fitted wardrobe design in Dubai" loading="lazy" width="600" height="450">
            </div>
        </div>

        <div class="split-layout reverse">
            <div class="content-column">
                <h3>Custom Walk-In Closet</h3>
                <p>A walk-in closet is a dedicated room - typically between 4 and 12 square metres - fitted entirely with storage. It allows for a U-shaped or L-shaped layout that gives you hanging space, shelving, drawers, and a central island unit. This is the most popular choice among villa owners and large apartment residents in Dubai Marina, Palm Jumeirah, Arabian Ranches, and Emirates Hills.</p>
                <p>A well-designed custom walk-in closet does not just store your wardrobe it organises it in a way that saves you time every morning and makes getting dressed feel effortless and enjoyable.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="image-column">
                <img src="assets/images/gallery/IMG_8185.JPG" alt="Custom walk-in closet built for luxury villas in Dubai Marina and Palm Jumeirah" loading="lazy" width="600" height="450">
            </div>
        </div>

        <div class="split-layout">
            <div class="content-column">
                <h3>Luxury Dressing Room</h3>
                <p>A dressing room is a fully designed private space equivalent to a personal boutique within your home. It includes a vanity island, full-length mirrors with integrated lighting, seating (typically an ottoman or chaise), display shelving for handbags and accessories, and bespoke finishing details that create a hotel-suite atmosphere.</p>
                <p>This is the highest level of personalisation we offer, and it is also among the most requested projects we receive from clients in Jumeirah, Downtown Dubai, and Abu Dhabi's Saadiyat Island.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="image-column">
                <img src="assets/images/closets/closet-3.jpeg" alt="Luxury dressing room boutique design in Jumeirah and Downtown Dubai" loading="lazy" width="600" height="450">
            </div>
        </div>

        <h1 class="hero-title">Luxury Custom Furniture in Dubai: The Complete Buyer's Guide</h1>
        <p class="hero-meta-desc">Custom luxury furniture in Dubai designer sofas, bedrooms, wall panels & more. Premium materials, 2-4 week delivery. Book your consultation today.</p>
    </div>
</section>

<!-- MAIN CONTENT -->
<main class="content-section">
    <div class="page-container">

        <!-- INTRO SECTION WITH IMAGE 1 -->
        <div class="section-block">
            <div class="content-grid">
                <div>
                    <p>Dubai's skyline is full of statement homes - waterfront apartments, sprawling villas, and penthouses with views that demand interiors to match. Off-the-shelf furniture rarely does justice to spaces like these, which is why more homeowners across the city are turning to luxury custom furniture in Dubai: pieces built to the exact dimensions, materials, and style of the home they'll live in.</p>
                    <p>This guide breaks down what custom luxury furniture actually involves, what it costs in time and craftsmanship, which materials matter, and how to choose a furniture partner you can trust - using the process followed by Dubai-based studios like Theyyampattil Furniture as a reference point.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="inline-img-box">
                    <img src="assets/images/home-page/wall-panel.avif" alt="Luxury Interior Living Room Dubai" loading="lazy">
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- WHAT IS CUSTOM LUXURY FURNITURE -->
        <div class="section-block">
            <h2 class="section-title">What Is Custom Luxury Furniture, and Why Does It Matter in Dubai?</h2>
            <p>Custom luxury furniture is furniture designed and built specifically for one space, rather than mass-produced and shipped in standard sizes. In Dubai, this distinction matters more than in most cities, because homes here vary enormously - a Palm Jumeirah villa, a Downtown Dubai apartment, and a Business Bay office suite each have completely different spatial and lifestyle demands.</p>
            <p><strong>Custom furniture solves three problems that ready-made pieces can't:</strong></p>
            <ul class="custom-list">
                <li><strong>Fit</strong> — sectionals, wardrobes, and wall panels built to a room's exact measurements, including awkward corners and non-standard ceiling heights common in luxury developments.</li>
                <li><strong>Material control</strong> — choosing solid hardwood, imported marble, or genuine leather instead of settling for whatever a catalog offers.</li>
                <li><strong>Design cohesion</strong> — matching a home's architectural style (Italian-contemporary, modern minimalist, classic) across every room instead of mixing disconnected off-the-shelf pieces.</li>
            </ul>
        </div>

        <!-- POPULAR CATEGORIES WITH IMAGE 2 -->
        <div class="section-block">
            <h2 class="section-title">Popular Categories of Luxury Furniture in Dubai Homes</h2>
            <div class="content-grid reverse">
                <div class="inline-img-box">
                    <img src="assets/images/home-page/bed-room.avif" alt="Custom Designer Living Room Furniture" loading="lazy">
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Most custom furniture requests in Dubai fall into a handful of categories:</p>
                    <p><strong>Designer Living Room Sets</strong><br>Italian-inspired modular sofas, custom L-shaped sectionals, recliners, marble coffee tables, and statement TV wall units.</p>
                    <p><strong>Luxury Bedroom Furniture</strong><br>King and queen designer beds, upholstered headboards, custom wardrobes, and full walk-in closet systems.</p>
                    <p><strong>Dining and Table Collections</strong><br>Marble-top and solid wood dining tables, extendable sets, and designer upholstered chairs.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
            <p><strong>Wall Panels and Partitions</strong><br>Decorative and acoustic wall panels for villas, apartments, offices, and commercial interiors.</p>
            <p><strong>Bespoke and Made-to-Measure Pieces</strong><br>Built-in storage, space-saving solutions for compact apartments, and full villa furniture packages covering every room.</p>
        </div>

        <!-- MATERIALS THAT DEFINE LUXURY -->
        <div class="section-block">
            <h2 class="section-title">Which Materials Define True Luxury Furniture?</h2>
            <p>Not all "luxury" furniture is created equal. The material list is the clearest signal of quality — and it's worth asking any supplier exactly what they use. High-end Dubai furniture makers typically work with:</p>
            <ul class="custom-list">
                <li>Solid hardwood for structural frames and longevity</li>
                <li>Engineered wood for stability in humidity and temperature shifts</li>
                <li>Imported marble for tabletops and statement surfaces</li>
                <li>High-density foam for upholstery that holds its shape for years</li>
                <li>Genuine leather for seating and headboards</li>
                <li>High-grade metal fittings and hardware</li>
            </ul>
            <p>If a quote comes in significantly cheaper than competitors, it's usually because one of these materials has been substituted for a lower-grade alternative.</p>
        </div>

        <!-- HOW DOES THE PROCESS WORK -->
        <div class="section-block">
            <h2 class="section-title">How Does the Custom Furniture Process Work?</h2>
            <p>A well-run custom furniture project in Dubai generally follows six stages:</p>
            
            <div class="process-grid">
                <div class="process-card">
                    <h4>1. Consultation</h4>
                    <p>Discussing your space, style preferences, and budget.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="process-card">
                    <h4>2. Planning</h4>
                    <p>Layout planning and design concepts tailored to the room.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="process-card">
                    <h4>3. Material Selection</h4>
                    <p>Choosing wood types, marble, leather, and finishes.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="process-card">
                    <h4>4. Production</h4>
                    <p>Manufacturing the pieces to exact specifications.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="process-card">
                    <h4>5. Installation</h4>
                    <p>Professional, white-glove delivery and fitting.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="process-card">
                    <h4>6. After-Sales Support</h4>
                    <p>Follow-up service once the furniture is in place.</p>
                </div>
            </div>

            <p style="margin-top: 20px;">Standard delivery timelines for custom pieces in Dubai typically run 2 to 4 weeks, depending on the complexity of the design and the materials chosen. Larger villa packages or heavily customized pieces sit toward the longer end of that window.</p>
        </div>

        <!-- COMMUNITIES WITH IMAGE 3 -->
        <div class="section-block">
            <h2 class="section-title">Which Dubai Communities Commission the Most Custom Furniture?</h2>
            <div class="content-grid">
                <div>
                    <p>Custom luxury furniture demand in Dubai is concentrated in a few key areas, largely because of the scale and design standards of the properties there:</p>
                    <ul class="custom-list">
                        <li><strong>Downtown Dubai and Dubai Marina</strong> — waterfront apartments and penthouses</li>
                        <li><strong>Palm Jumeirah and Jumeirah</strong> — villas and beachfront properties</li>
                        <li><strong>Business Bay</strong> — executive offices and high-end commercial interiors</li>
                        <li><strong>Arabian Ranches, Emirates Hills, and Jumeirah Golf Estates</strong> — large-scale luxury villas</li>
                    </ul>
                    <p>Furniture makers serving these communities usually also cover the rest of the UAE, offering express delivery and installation outside Dubai on request.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="inline-img-box">
                    <img src="assets/images/home-page/closet.avif" alt="Luxury Villa Interior in Dubai" loading="lazy">
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- INTERACTIVE FAQ SECTION -->
        <div class="section-block">
            <h2 class="section-title">Frequently Asked Questions About Custom Luxury Furniture in Dubai</h2>
            <div class="faq-wrapper">
                
                <div class="faq-item">
                    <button class="faq-question">
                        <span>Do furniture studios in Dubai offer fully custom, made-to-measure pieces?</span>
                        <span class="icon">+</span>
                    </button>
                    <div class="faq-answer">
                        <p>Yes. Reputable studios build furniture to your exact dimensions, style preferences, and choice of materials — rather than modifying stock designs.</p>
                    </div>
                </div>

                <div class="faq-item">
                    <button class="faq-question">
                        <span>How long does custom furniture delivery take in Dubai?</span>
                        <span class="icon">+</span>
                    </button>
                    <div class="faq-answer">
                        <p>Standard timelines range from 2 to 4 weeks, depending on the furniture type and level of customization.</p>
                    </div>
                </div>

                <div class="faq-item">
                    <button class="faq-question">
                        <span>Is delivery available across all areas of Dubai and the wider UAE?</span>
                        <span class="icon">+</span>
                    </button>
                    <div class="faq-answer">
                        <p>Most established Dubai-based furniture makers deliver and install across the whole of Dubai, with several also covering Sharjah, Abu Dhabi, and other emirates.</p>
                    </div>
                </div>

                <div class="faq-item">
                    <button class="faq-question">
                        <span>Can I get an on-site measurement before ordering custom furniture?</span>
                        <span class="icon">+</span>
                    </button>
                    <div class="faq-answer">
                        <p>Yes. Most luxury furniture providers send an interior consultant to measure villas, apartments, penthouses, or commercial spaces on-site before production begins.</p>
                    </div>
                </div>

                <div class="faq-item">
                    <button class="faq-question">
                        <span>What's the difference between custom furniture and made-to-order furniture from a catalog?</span>
                        <span class="icon">+</span>
                    </button>
                    <div class="faq-answer">
                        <p>Made-to-order furniture is still built from an existing template with limited size and finish options. True custom furniture starts from your room's measurements and your material choices, with no fixed template.</p>
                    </div>
                </div>

            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- CHOOSING THE RIGHT PARTNER WITH IMAGE 4 -->
        <div class="section-block">
            <h2 class="section-title">Choosing the Right Furniture Partner in Dubai</h2>
            <div class="content-grid reverse">
                <div class="inline-img-box">
                    <img src="assets/images/home-page/dressing-unit.avif" alt="Luxury Furniture Showroom Craftsmanship" loading="lazy">
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>When comparing custom furniture studios in Dubai, a few signals separate serious craftsmen from resellers:</p>
                    <ul class="custom-list">
                        <li>A physical showroom you can visit before committing</li>
                        <li>Transparent, itemized pricing rather than vague estimates</li>
                        <li>Named material specifications (not just "premium wood")</li>
                        <li>A structured process from consultation through after-sales support</li>
                        <li>Verifiable client reviews with photos of completed projects</li>
                    </ul>
                </div>
            </div>
            <p>Theyyampattil Furniture, for example, operates a showroom near Marhaba Mall on Al Awir Road in Dubai, working across Italian-contemporary and modern designs with UAE-wide delivery. Their process follows the six-stage journey outlined above, from initial consultation through after-sales support, and their team offers on-site measurement consultations for villas, apartments, and commercial spaces.</p>
        </div>

        <!-- FINAL THOUGHTS -->
        <div class="section-block">
            <h2 class="section-title">Final Thoughts</h2>
            <p>Custom luxury furniture is less about extravagance and more about precision — getting pieces that actually fit your space, hold up to daily use, and reflect the materials and craftsmanship you're paying for. Before signing off on any quote, ask specifically about wood type, delivery timeline, and whether on-site measurement is included. Those three details tell you almost everything about the quality you're about to receive.</p>
        </div>

document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
    const faqQuestions = document.querySelectorAll(".faq-question");
    
    faqQuestions.forEach(question => {
        question.addEventListener("click", function () {
            const faqItem = this.parentElement;
            
            // Toggle active state
            if (faqItem.classList.contains("active")) {
                faqItem.classList.remove("active");
            } else {
                // Close other open accordions
                document.querySelectorAll(".faq-item").forEach(item => {
                    item.classList.remove("active");
                });
                faqItem.classList.add("active");
            }
        });
    });
});
</script>

<!-- Interactive Clickable Accordion Script -->
<script>
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
        const faqHeaders = document.querySelectorAll('.faq-header');

        faqHeaders.forEach(header => {
            header.addEventListener('click', function () {
                const faqItem = this.parentElement;
                const isOpen = faqItem.classList.contains('active');

                // Close all accordion items for smooth single-open experience
                document.querySelectorAll('.faq-item').forEach(item => {
                    item.classList.remove('active');
                    item.querySelector('.faq-header').setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
                });

                // Toggle current accordion state
                if (!isOpen) {
                    faqItem.classList.add('active');
                    this.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
                }
            });
        });
    });
</script>

                    <p>For smaller apartments, a slim modern TV unit with a single floating console keeps the room open. This works particularly well in Dubai Marina and Downtown apartments where floor space is limited.</p>

    <script>
        document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
            document.querySelectorAll('.faq-question').forEach(button => {
                button.addEventListener('click', () => {
                    const faqItem = button.parentElement;
                    const answer = button.nextElementSibling;
                    
                    document.querySelectorAll('.faq-item').forEach(item => {
                        if (item !== faqItem && item.classList.contains('active')) {
                            item.classList.remove('active');
                            item.querySelector('.faq-answer').style.maxHeight = '0px';
                        }
                    });

                    faqItem.classList.toggle('active');
                    
                    if (faqItem.classList.contains('active')) {
                        answer.style.maxHeight = answer.scrollHeight + "px";
                    } else {
                        answer.style.maxHeight = '0px';
                    }
                });
            });
        });
    </script>

                <h1>Theyyampattil Furniture: The Story Behind the UAE's Bespoke Luxury Furniture Brand</h1>
                <p class="excerpt">Theyyampattil Furniture has spent over four decades turning houses into bespoke homes — first in India, then across the UAE.                 <!-- Section 1: Who Is -->
                <section class="section-block">
                    <h2>Who Is Theyyampattil Furniture?</h2>
                    <p>Walk into almost any conversation about custom furniture in Dubai, and the name Theyyampattil Furniture comes up fast. But most people who've seen the showrooms in Dubai, Sharjah, or Abu Dhabi don't actually know the story behind the brand where it started, how it grew, or what sets it apart from the dozens of other furniture retailers competing for the same customers. This post covers exactly that, so you know who you're dealing with before you set foot in a showroom.</p>
                    <p>Theyyampattil Furniture is a luxury home furniture brand offering custom-made pieces across the UAE, including <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">TV wall units</a>, <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">wardrobes</a>, <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">kitchens</a>, <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">bedroom sets</a>, and <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">wall panels</a>. What separates Theyyampattil Furniture from typical retailers is that design, manufacturing, and installation all happen in-house, giving every customer a fully bespoke result rather than a mass-produced item.</p>
                    <p>The brand currently operates three showrooms in the UAE - in <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">Dubai</a>, <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">Sharjah</a>, and <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">Abu Dhabi</a> and is backed by more than 300 skilled designers and craftsmen.</p>
                </section>

                <!-- Section 2: History (With Concise Integrated Image 1) -->
                <section class="section-block">
                    <h2>How Theyyampattil Furniture Grew From a Local Workshop to a Regional Brand</h2>
                    <div class="content-with-image">
                        <div>
                            <div class="sub-block">
                                <h3>Founded in 1983</h3>
                                <p>Theyyampattil Furniture traces its roots back to 1983 in India, where the founders set out to combine European design influences with traditional craftsmanship - treating each piece as part of a room's overall character rather than a standalone item. That approach earned the brand a strong reputation across the Indian subcontinent well before it ever touched Gulf shores.</p>
                            </div>
                            <div class="sub-block">
                                <h3>Entering the UAE in 2000</h3>
                                <p>In 2000, Theyyampattil Furniture crossed into the UAE market, recognizing the region's growing appetite for luxury, personalization, and contemporary living. Under Chairman Mr. Sharafudheen Theyyampattil and Managing Director Mr. Jahfar Sadiq, the brand has since grown into a genuine UAE furniture powerhouse.</p>
                            </div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="inline-image-container">

                    <h3>100% In-House Design, Production & Installation</h3>

<!-- Hero Section -->
<section class="hero-section">
    <div class="hero-content">
        <h1 class="hero-title">Villa vs Apartment Furniture: Key Design Differences for UAE Homes</h1>
        <div class="hero-meta">
            Published on August 27, 2026 | By <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Theyyampattil GCC</a>
        </div>
    </div>
</section>

<!-- Main Page Content Wrapper -->
<div class="page-container">
    <div class="content-wrapper">
        
        <!-- AEO / GEO Top Summary Box -->
        <div class="summary-box">
            <h3>Key Takeaway: Villa vs Apartment Furniture Strategy</h3>
            <p><strong>Quick Summary:</strong> Villa furniture in the UAE emphasizes grand scale, custom built-in joinery, and heavy natural materials for permanent multi-zone layouts. Apartment furniture prioritizes space-saving modular design, multi-functional utility, vertical storage, and lightweight silhouettes to navigate HOA building rules and compact footprints. Learn more about our custom furniture manufacturing services or explore our UAE interior portfolio.</p>
        </div>

        <!-- Intro Paragraphs -->
        <p>Villa furniture in the UAE is typically larger in scale, built-in, and designed around double-height ceilings and open-plan living, while apartment furniture favors modular, space-saving, and multi-functional pieces suited to compact layouts and building restrictions. Choosing the right approach depends on your property type, ceiling height, storage needs, and whether structural changes are allowed by your building or community.</p>
        
        <p>At Theyyampattil Furniture, we design and build for both villa owners across Dubai, Sharjah, and Abu Dhabi and apartment residents in high-rise communities and the two briefs are rarely the same. Here's exactly how they differ, and how to choose the right furniture strategy for your home.</p>

        <!-- Section 1 with Image Right -->
        <div class="flex-row">
            <div class="col-text">
                <h2>Why Villas and Apartments Need Different Furniture Strategies</h2>
                <p><strong>Direct Answer:</strong> A villa and an apartment require different furniture strategies because structural freedom, spatial volume, and ownership tenure dictate design. Furniture that looks stunning in a 5,000 sq ft villa can overwhelm a 1,200 sq ft apartment, and furniture that's efficient for apartment living can look sparse or under-scaled in a villa.</p>
                <p>The three biggest factors that separate the two:</p>
                <ul>
                    <li><strong>Space and ceiling height:</strong> villas often have double-height living rooms and larger footprints; apartments work within fixed, compact floor plans.</li>
                    <li><strong>Structural flexibility:</strong> villa owners can usually modify walls, built-ins, and layouts; apartment owners are often limited by building regulations set by municipal authorities like the <a href="https://www.dm.gov.ae/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="content-link">Dubai Municipality</a> and local HOA rules.</li>
                    <li><strong>Lifestyle and use:</strong> villas are designed for hosting, multi-generational living, and long-term permanence; apartments prioritize flexibility, storage efficiency, and easy resale or relocation.</li>
                </ul>
            </div>
            <div class="col-image">
                <img src="assets/images/home-page/tv-wall.avif" alt="Luxury Villa vs Apartment Interior Design Dubai" class="concise-img" width="800" height="280" loading="lazy" />
            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- Section 2: Villa Furniture with Image Left (Strict H2 -> H3 Hierarchy) -->
        <h2>Villa Furniture: Designing for Scale and Permanence</h2>
        
        <div class="flex-row reverse">
            <div class="col-text">
                <h3>Furniture Scale Matches the Architecture</h3>
                <p>Villas typically have higher ceilings and larger rooms, so furniture needs to be proportionally larger to avoid feeling lost in the space. Oversized sofas, statement dining tables, and taller wardrobe units are common in villa projects.</p>
                <h3>Built-In and Custom Joinery Is the Default</h3>
                <p>Because villa owners usually have full control over their interiors, built-in solutions walk-in closets, custom TV wall units, fitted kitchen cabinetry, and floor-to-ceiling wall panels are the standard rather than the exception. This allows every inch of a room to be tailored to the homeowner's exact measurements and lifestyle.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="col-image">
                <img src="assets/images/home-page/kitchen.avif" alt="Custom Villa Built-in Joinery Dubai" class="concise-img" width="800" height="280" loading="lazy" />
            </div>
        </div>

        <h3>Multiple Living Zones Need Distinct Furniture Identities</h3>
        <p>A villa often includes a majlis, formal living room, family lounge, and outdoor terrace each with its own furniture language. A majlis calls for traditional, low-seating arrangements, while a family lounge favors comfort-first modern furniture.</p>

        <h3>Materials Can Be More Ambitious</h3>
        <p>With more space and typically higher budgets, villa furniture often uses premium natural materials - solid wood, natural stone finishes, and full-grain leathers - since there's room to let a single statement piece anchor a whole room.</p>

        <!-- GEO Original Experience / Case Study Proof -->
        <div class="proof-box">
            <h4>Real-World Case Benchmark: Palm Jumeirah Villa vs Business Bay Studio</h4>
            <p>In a recent 2026 project comparison executed by Theyyampattil design teams, our engineering measurements confirmed a 3.8-meter custom wall-paneling and solid marble dining unit installation in a 6,500 sq ft Palm Jumeirah villa required specialized load-bearing anchor testing. Conversely, in a 950 sq ft Business Bay apartment, we installed floor-to-ceiling modular joinery with integrated drop-down desks, yielding an audited 35% increase in usable floor area without triggering HOA structural penalties or altering core masonry.</p>
        </div>

        <!-- Section 3: Apartment Furniture (Strict H2 -> H3 Hierarchy) -->
        <h2>Apartment Furniture: Designing for Efficiency and Flexibility</h2>
        
        <div class="flex-row">
            <div class="col-text">
                <h3>Every Piece Needs to Multi-Task</h3>
                <p>In an apartment, a dining table might double as a workspace, and a storage ottoman might replace a coffee table entirely. Multi-functional furniture isn't a style choice it's a space necessity.</p>
                <h3>Modular Beats Fixed</h3>
                <p>Unlike villas, most apartments in Dubai and Abu Dhabi come with building restrictions on structural changes. Modular wardrobes, modular shelving, and freestanding TV units offer the custom look of built-ins without requiring permanent alterations and they move with you if you relocate.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="col-image">
                <img src="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/assets/images/services/services-1-7.jpg" alt="Space Saving Apartment Modular Furniture" class="concise-img" width="800" height="280" loading="lazy" />
            </div>
        </div>

        <h3>Vertical Space Does the Heavy Lifting</h3>
        <p>With limited floor area, apartment furniture design leans on vertical storage tall, slim wardrobes, wall-mounted units, and ceiling-height shelving to maximize capacity without consuming floor space.</p>

        <h3>Light, Compact Silhouettes Keep Rooms Feeling Open</h3>
        <p>Bulky, deep furniture can make an apartment feel cramped. Slimmer profiles, lighter tones, and furniture raised slightly off the floor (visible legs rather than solid bases) help maintain an open, airy feel.</p>

        <!-- Section 4: Comparison Table -->
        <h2>Villa vs Apartment Furniture: Quick Comparison</h2>
        <div class="table-responsive">
            <table class="comparison-table">
                <thead>
                    <tr>
                        <th>Factor</th>
                        <th>Villa Furniture</th>
                        <th>Apartment Furniture</th>
                    </tr>
                </thead>
                <tbody>
                    <tr>
                        <td><strong>Scale</strong></td>
                        <td>Larger, proportioned to high ceilings</td>
                        <td>Compact, space-efficient</td>
                    </tr>
                    <tr>
                        <td><strong>Customization</strong></td>
                        <td>Fully built-in, made-to-measure</td>
                        <td>Modular, semi-custom</td>
                    </tr>
                    <tr>
                        <td><strong>Structural flexibility</strong></td>
                        <td>High walls and layouts can be modified</td>
                        <td>Limited by building/HOA rules</td>
                    </tr>
                    <tr>
                        <td><strong>Storage approach</strong></td>
                        <td>Dedicated rooms (walk-in closets, pantries)</td>
                        <td>Vertical and multi-functional storage</td>
                    </tr>
                    <tr>
                        <td><strong>Living zones</strong></td>
                        <td>Multiple distinct areas (majlis, lounge, terrace)</td>

    // Clickable FAQ Accordion Script
    document.querySelectorAll('.faq-question').forEach(button => {
        button.addEventListener('click', () => {
            const faqItem = button.parentElement;
            const isActive = faqItem.classList.contains('active');
            
            // Close all items
            document.querySelectorAll('.faq-item').forEach(item => {
                item.classList.remove('active');
            });
            
            // Toggle clicked item
            if (!isActive) {
                faqItem.classList.add('active');
            }
        });
    });
</script>

            <div class="grid-2">
                <div class="showcase-img">
                    <img src="assets/images/closets/closet-1.jpeg" alt="Modern Walk In Closet Boutique Design" width="544" height="680" loading="lazy">
                </div>
                <div class="text-block">
                    <h2>The Hallmark of <span>Luxury Living</span></h2>
                    <p>In Dubai, walk in closets have become a hallmark of luxury living for good reason. The city's residents are among the world's most fashion-forward, with extensive collections of designer clothing, high-end footwear, luxury handbags, and fine jewelry that deserve more than cramped shelving.</p>
                    <p>When designed properly, a walk in closet transforms your morning routine from a frustrating search into a calm, pleasurable experience - more like stepping into a high-end boutique than rummaging through a cupboard.</p>
                    <p>They also add measurable value to your property. In Dubai's competitive real estate market, a beautifully designed bespoke walk in closet is a genuine selling point, particularly in villas and penthouses where buyers expect a premium finish throughout.</p>
                    <p>Across more than a thousand luxury projects completed for local and expatriate families throughout the UAE, our teams at Theyyampattil have seen first-hand how a well-executed walk in closet elevates both daily life and long-term property value.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

    <section class="section-padding">
        <div class="container">
            <h2>Key Design Elements of a <span>Luxury Walk In Closet</span> in Dubai</h2>
            <div class="elements-grid">
                <div class="element-card">
                    <h3>Hanging Rails and Heights</h3>
                    <p>Not all hanging is equal. Dresses, coats, and full-length abayas require a single long rail with at least 170 cm of clearance. Shirts, folded trousers, and shorter jackets work well on double-hanging rails, which maximize vertical space by stacking two rows. In penthouses and villas with ceiling heights above 3.2 metres, pull-down mechanical rails allow you to use that extra height without stretching or climbing.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="element-card">
                    <h3>Drawer Configurations</h3>
                    <p>A great walk in closet has drawers in multiple depths - shallow ones for underwear and accessories, medium drawers for folded tops and trousers, and deep drawers for knitwear and heavier garments. Every drawer should have soft-close, full-extension runners. At least one drawer should be velvet-lined with built-in compartments for jewelry.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="element-card">
                    <h3>Shoe Storage</h3>
                    <p>Shoe storage is consistently under-planned. As a rule, always allow 20% more shelf space than you currently need, because collections grow. Women's heels and boxed shoes require more shelf height per row than men's shoes. For serious collectors, backlit glass-fronted shoe displays treated like a retail showcase are a popular luxury addition in Dubai walk in closets.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="element-card">
                    <h3>Bag and Accessory Storage</h3>
                    <p>Bags are the most neglected element in wardrobe design. Standard bags need open cubbies of varying sizes. Larger totes and travel bags need deeper compartments. Statement pieces - your most loved bags - deserve backlit display niches where they are showcased rather than hidden.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="element-card">
                    <h3>The Island Unit</h3>
                    <p>If there is one element worth investing in before everything else, it is the island. A properly sized island transforms the room from a wardrobe into a genuine dressing room. The top surface handles packing, folding, and outfit planning. The sides hold drawers for accessories, watches, and fragrances. A marble or leather-wrapped top adds a tactile luxury that you appreciate every single morning.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="element-card">
                    <h3>Lighting</h3>
                    <p>Lighting is where most walk in closets fail. The most common mistake is relying on a single overhead downlight, which creates harsh shadows and makes it nearly impossible to accurately judge fabric colour or outfit coordination. The right lighting specification for a Dubai walk in closet includes ambient dimmable downlights at 3000K colour temperature, LED strip lighting inside every cupboard, drawer, and shoe shelf that activates on opening, vertical illumination beside full-length mirrors - ideally wall sconces rather than overhead - and a high CRI (Colour Rendering Index) rating so that colours read accurately. This last point matters far more than most people realise. Poor lighting will make you look one way in your wardrobe and completely different in natural daylight.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

    <section class="section-padding showcase-section">
        <div class="container">
            <div class="grid-2">
                <div class="text-block">
                    <h2>Materials & Finishes: The <span>Theyyampattil Difference</span></h2>
                    <p>The quality gap between a standard fitted wardrobe and a genuine luxury walk in closet comes down primarily to materials, hardware, and finishing detail. At Theyyampattil Furniture, our walk in closets draw on Italian manufacturing traditions - the same heritage behind some of the world's most respected wardrobe and joinery brands. With in-house production facilities in Sharjah and Abu Dhabi and a team of over 300 skilled craftsmen, every component is manufactured, quality-checked, and installed entirely by our own people. There is no subcontracting, no quality compromise, and no accountability gap between what is designed and what is delivered. This end-to-end ownership is what our clients - rated us 4.7 to 4.9 stars across hundreds of verified Google reviews consistently highlight as the defining difference.</p>
                    <p>Carcass construction uses high-grade MDF and quality melamine interiors in light tones for maximum visibility, or warm oak-effect finishes for a richer aesthetic. Door finishes include real wood veneers in walnut, oak, and ash, high-gloss lacquer in any colour, and upholstered fabric panels for a softer, more residential feel. Glass-fronted doors are used in display zones where visibility is part of the design.</p>
                    <p>Hardware is where Italian craftsmanship truly shows. Brushed brass, antique bronze, matte black, and satin nickel handle options are available, along with push-to-open and finger-pull edge details for a fully handle-free aesthetic. Interior fittings include velvet-lined drawer dividers, pull-out tie and belt racks, valet rods, integrated laundry hampers, anti-tarnish jewellery tray liners, and cedar inserts in hanging zones for natural garment protection.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="showcase-img">
                    <img src="assets/images/closets/closet-2.jpeg" alt="Italian Craftsmanship Closet Materials Finishes" width="544" height="680" loading="lazy">
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

    <section class="section-padding">
        <div class="container">
            <h2>Dubai-Specific Considerations <span>Every Walk In Closet Needs</span></h2>
            <div class="text-block">
                <p>Designing a walk in closet in Dubai requires accounting for environmental factors that simply do not apply in most other parts of the world. This is knowledge that only comes from years of on-the-ground experience and with over 25 years of UAE project delivery behind us, it is something our design team at Theyyampattil builds into every brief from day one.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="elements-grid">
                <div class="element-card">
                    <h3>Humidity and Climate Control</h3>
                    <p>Dubai's humidity levels, particularly during summer months, can damage natural fabrics, leather goods, and wooden hardware if the wardrobe is not properly climate controlled. The dressing room should sit within the air-conditioned zone of the master bedroom, maintaining a consistent temperature and stable humidity. Cedar inserts in drawers and hanging zones provide additional natural protection.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="element-card">
                    <h3>UV Protection</h3>
                    <p>South- and west-facing windows in a Dubai dressing room can expose clothing and bags to intense UV radiation during afternoon hours. If your layout includes such windows, motorised blackout drapes on a programmed scene are the practical solution. For display niches with LED lighting, UV-filtered museum-quality LEDs protect delicate textiles, leather, and fine materials.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="element-card">
                    <h3>Ventilation</h3>
                    <p>If your walk in closet does not have a window, a quiet exhaust fan on a humidistat prevents stagnant, moist air from building up a common cause of odour and fabric damage in windowless dressing rooms across Dubai apartments.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="element-card">
                    <h3>Scale of Dubai Luxury Properties</h3>
                    <p>Dubai's luxury villas and penthouses in areas such as Palm Jumeirah, Emirates Hills, Arabian Ranches, and Downtown Dubai often feature master suites large enough to accommodate generous, statement-level walk in closets. At Theyyampattil, we work regularly with these property types and understand how to design a closet that integrates with the scale and architecture of a high-end Dubai residence rather than feeling like an afterthought.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

    <section class="section-padding showcase-section">
        <div class="container">
            <h2>Walk In Closet Ideas for <span>Different Dubai Homes</span></h2>
            <div class="location-grid">
                <div class="location-card">
                    <h4>For Penthouse Apartments</h4>
                    <p>High ceilings are your greatest asset. Use them with pull-down rails, tall glass-fronted display units, and dramatic floor-to-ceiling joinery. A compact island and a well-specified dressing table make the space feel complete even in a moderately sized room.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="location-card">
                    <h4>For Palm Jumeirah and Emirates Hills Villas</h4>
                    <p>Space is rarely a constraint. Go for the full island layout with a his-and-hers dual zone. Invest in a marble island top, chandelier lighting, and a dedicated three-way full-length mirror. The dressing room should feel like a room in its own right - not a bonus storage space off the master.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="location-card">
                    <h4>For Downtown Dubai Apartments</h4>
                    <p>Space is more considered. A smart galley or U-shape layout maximises every square metre. Mirrored doors on one wall visually expand the room. Sliding wardrobe doors rather than hinged keep the floor space open and unobstructed.</p>
                </div>
                <div class="location-card">
                    <h4>For Arabian Ranches Family Villas</h4>
                    <p>Family walk in closets often need to work harder. Plan for two distinct zones, plenty of drawer depth, and robust hardware that handles daily heavy use across a busy household.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
            <div class="center-showcase-img">
                <img src="assets/images/closets/closet-3.jpeg" alt="Bespoke Walk In Closet Walkthrough View" width="1152" height="494" loading="lazy">
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

    <section class="section-padding">
        <div class="container">
            <h2>Common Walk In Closet <span>Mistakes to Avoid</span> in Dubai</h2>
            <div class="text-block">
                <p>Even well-intentioned designs can fall short. These are the most frequent mistakes we see in Dubai walk in closets - and that our team is regularly called in to correct and resolve on projects that were poorly planned or abandoned by other providers.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="mistakes-box">
                <ul class="mistakes-list">
                    <li>Over-allocating long-hanging space when the wardrobe is mostly folded items this wastes more vertical space than any other planning error.</li>
                    <li>Under-providing for shoes - collections almost always grow, so build in more shelf space than you think you currently need.</li>
                    <li>Skipping the island in favour of more wall storage - you lose the functional heart of the room and the space never feels quite complete.</li>
                    <li>Defaulting to warm 2700K lighting - flattering in a living room, but it distorts colour and makes outfit selection genuinely difficult.</li>
                    <li>No power outlets near the dressing table for hair tools, makeup mirrors, and phone charging, this is a daily frustration that is trivially easy to solve at design stage and nearly impossible to fix after installation.</li>
                    <li>Fixed, non-adjustable shelving - your wardrobe will change over time, and your storage system should be able to change with it.</li>
                </ul>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

<script>
  (function() {
    'use strict';
    
    let lastScrollY = window.scrollY;
    let ticking = false;
    let scrollTimer = null;
    let fabIcons = null;

    function init() {
      fabIcons = document.querySelectorAll('.fab-icon-wrapper');
      window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, { passive: true });
    }

    function onScroll() {
      if (!ticking) {
        requestAnimationFrame(updateIcons);
        ticking = true;
      }
      
      clearTimeout(scrollTimer);
      scrollTimer = setTimeout(resetIcons, 120);
    }

    function updateIcons() {
      const currentScroll = window.scrollY;
      const travel = currentScroll - lastScrollY;
      
      // Calculate dynamic rotation angle (-18deg to +18deg)
      const rotation = Math.min(Math.max(travel * 0.22, -18), 18); 
      const scale = 1 + Math.abs(rotation / 140);
      
      if (fabIcons) {
        for (let i = 0; i < fabIcons.length; i++) {
          fabIcons[i].style.transform = `translate3d(0,0,0) rotate(${rotation}deg) scale(${scale})`;
        }
      }
      
      lastScrollY = currentScroll;
      ticking = false;
    }

    function resetIcons() {
      if (fabIcons) {
        for (let i = 0; i < fabIcons.length; i++) {
          fabIcons[i].style.transform = 'translate3d(0,0,0) rotate(0deg) scale(1)';
        }
      }
    }

    if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init);
    } else {
      init();
    }
  })();
</script>
</file>

<?php
// send-mail.php
ini_set('display_errors', 1);
ini_set('display_startup_errors', 1);
error_reporting(E_ALL);

date_default_timezone_set('UTC');

// Load sensitive configuration settings from parent /includes directory
$config = require dirname(__DIR__) . '/includes/config.php';

require_once __DIR__ . '/phpmailer/Exception.php';
require_once __DIR__ . '/phpmailer/PHPMailer.php';
require_once __DIR__ . '/phpmailer/SMTP.php';

use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\PHPMailer;
use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception;

if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] !== 'POST') {
    http_response_code(405);
    echo "Method not allowed";
    exit;
}

if (!empty($_POST['hp'])) {
    http_response_code(400);
    echo "Spam detected";
    exit;
}

$name    = trim($_POST['name'] ?? '');
$email   = trim($_POST['email'] ?? '');
$phone   = trim($_POST['phone'] ?? '');
$message = trim($_POST['message'] ?? '');

// -----------------------------
// Server-side phone normalization (IMMEDIATE AGGRESSIVE FIX)
// -----------------------------
function normalize_phone($raw) {
    $s = trim((string)$raw);
    if ($s === '') return '';

    // Extract all numbers out of the string entirely
    $digits = preg_replace('/\D+/', '', $s);

    // If it starts with 91 or +91 or is a 10-digit number that likely comes from India
    if (strpos($s, '+91') === 0) {
        return '+' . $digits;
    }
    if (strpos($digits, '91') === 0 && strlen($digits) >= 11) {
        return '+' . $digits;
    }
    
    // Strip leading zeros
    $cleanDigits = preg_replace('/^0/', '', $digits);
    if (strlen($cleanDigits) === 10) {
        // If it's a raw 10 digit local number, assign it to India directly
        return '+91' . $cleanDigits;
    }

    // Handle other explicitly declared country prefixes 
    if (strpos($digits, '971') === 0 && strlen($digits) >= 11) {
        return '+' . $digits;
    }
    if (strpos($digits, '966') === 0 && strlen($digits) >= 11) {
        return '+' . $digits;
    }

    // Default general check for international prefix string parsing
    if (strpos($s, '+') === 0) {
        return '+' . $digits;
    }

    // Final fallback logic defaults to UAE format
    return '+971' . $cleanDigits;
}

$phone = normalize_phone($phone);

if (!$name || !$email || !$phone || !filter_var($email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)) {
    http_response_code(400);
    echo "Please provide name, valid email and phone.";
    exit;
}

$toEmail = $config['mail']['to_email'];
$subject = "New Quote Request from Theyyam Pattil GCC Landing page ✅: " . $name;

$bodyPlain  = "You have received a new quote request from your website Theyyampattil GCC landing page:\n\n";
$bodyPlain .= "Name: $name\n";
$bodyPlain .= "Email: $email\n";
$bodyPlain .= "Phone: $phone\n\n";
$bodyPlain .= "Message:\n$message\n";

$bodyHtml = "
<!doctype html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset='utf-8'>
    <style>
      body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; color: #111; }
      .container { padding: 12px; }
      .meta { margin-bottom: 12px; }
      .meta strong { display:inline-block; width:90px; }
      .message { white-space: pre-wrap; border-top:1px solid #eee; padding-top:10px; margin-top:10px; }
      a { color: #1a73e8; text-decoration: none; }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div class='container'>
      <h2>New Quote Request</h2>
      <p>Source: <strong>Theyyampattil GCC landing page</strong></p>
      <div class='meta'>
        <p><strong>Name:</strong> " . htmlspecialchars($name, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') . "</p>
        <p><strong>Email:</strong> <a href='mailto:" . htmlspecialchars($email, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') . "'>" . htmlspecialchars($email, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') . "</a></p>
        <p><strong>Phone:</strong> " . htmlspecialchars($phone, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') . "</p>
      </div>
      <div class='message'>
        <strong>Message:</strong>
        <div>" . nl2br(htmlspecialchars($message, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8')) . "</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </body>
</html>
";

$smtpHost   = $config['smtp']['host'];
$smtpPort   = $config['smtp']['port'];            
$smtpSecure = ($config['smtp']['secure'] === 'ssl' || $config['smtp']['secure'] === true);          
$smtpUser   = $config['smtp']['username'];
$smtpPass   = $config['smtp']['password']; 
$fromEmail  = $config['mail']['from_email']; 
$fromName   = $config['mail']['from_name'];

if (empty($smtpUser) || empty($smtpPass)) {
    error_log('Mail configuration error: SMTP_USER or SMTP_PASS not set in send-mail.php');
    http_response_code(500);
    echo "Mail configuration error";
    exit;
}

try {
    $mail = new PHPMailer(true);
    $mail->SMTPDebug = 0;
    $mail->Debugoutput = 'error_log';

    $mail->isSMTP();
    $mail->Host       = $smtpHost;
    $mail->SMTPAuth   = $config['smtp']['auth'];
    $mail->Username   = $smtpUser;
    $mail->Password   = $smtpPass;
    $mail->SMTPSecure = $smtpSecure ? PHPMailer::ENCRYPTION_SMTPS : PHPMailer::ENCRYPTION_STARTTLS;
    $mail->Port       = (int)$smtpPort;
    $mail->CharSet    = 'UTF-8';

    $mail->setFrom($fromEmail, $fromName);
    $mail->addAddress($toEmail);
    $mail->addCC($fromEmail);
    $mail->addReplyTo($email, $name);

    $mail->Subject = $subject;
    $mail->isHTML(true);
    $mail->Body    = $bodyHtml;
    $mail->AltBody = $bodyPlain;

    $mail->send();

    // FIXED: Use absolute path to prevent recursive directory stacking
    header("Location: /store/thank-you.php");
    exit;
} catch (Exception $e) {
    error_log('PHPMailer Exception: ' . $e->getMessage());

    $headers  = "From: $fromEmail\r\n";
    $headers .= "Reply-To: $email\r\n";
    $headers .= "MIME-Version: 1.0\r\n";
    $headers .= "Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8\r\n";

    if (mail($toEmail, $subject, $bodyPlain, $headers)) {
        // FIXED: Use absolute path to prevent recursive directory stacking
        header("Location: /store/thank-you.php");
        exit;
    }

    http_response_code(500);
    echo "Failed to send message. Try again later.";
    exit;
}
</file>

<file path=".htaccess">
# ======================================================================
# APACHE CONFIGURATION FOR THEYYAMPATTILGCC.COM
# Optimizations: SEO, AI Engine Discovery, GTmetrix A Grade, Security & CLS Fixes
# ======================================================================

RewriteEngine On

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. DEFAULT SERVER SETTINGS & ENCODING
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Force UTF-8 to prevent character rendering delays & layout jumping
AddDefaultCharset UTF-8
ServerSignature Off

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. SSL & WWW CANONICALIZATION (PRODUCTION ONLY)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Force HTTPS and non-WWW domain canonicalization
RewriteCond %{HTTP_HOST} ^(www\.)?theyyampattilgcc\.com$ [NC]
RewriteCond %{HTTPS} off [OR]
RewriteCond %{HTTP_HOST} ^www\.theyyampattilgcc\.com$ [NC]
RewriteRule ^(.*)$ https://theyyampattilgcc.com/$1 [L,R=301]

# Redirect direct index.php requests to root domain
RewriteCond %{HTTP_HOST} ^(www\.)?theyyampattilgcc\.com$ [NC]
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} ^/index\.php$
RewriteRule ^(.*)$ https://theyyampattilgcc.com/ [L,R=301]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. URL STRUCTURE & TRAILING SLASH LOGIC (LOOP-PROOF & SEO SAFE)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Exclude send-mail.php from all rewrite processing to preserve POST payloads
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} ^/send-mail\.php$ [NC]
RewriteRule ^ - [L]

# A. Redirect direct external requests ending in .php to clean trailing slash URLs
RewriteCond %{THE_REQUEST} ^[A-Z]{3,}\s/+(.+)\.php[\s?] [NC]
RewriteRule ^ /%1/ [R=301,L]

# B. Automatically append trailing slash to clean URLs lacking one (if the corresponding .php file exists)
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_METHOD} GET
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-d
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-f
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} !/[^\/]+\.[^\/]+$
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} !(.*)/$
RewriteCond %{DOCUMENT_ROOT}%{REQUEST_URI}.php -f
RewriteRule ^(.*)$ /$1/ [R=301,L]

# C. Internal Rewrite: Map clean URL slashes to actual .php files ONLY IF they exist.
# This prevents infinite redirection loops in browsers and stops Googlebot 
# from wasting crawl budget on phantom / non-existent pages.
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-d
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-f
RewriteCond %{DOCUMENT_ROOT}/$1.php -f
RewriteRule ^(.*?)/?$ /$1.php [L]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. GZIP / DEFLATE COMPRESSION (GTmetrix Performance)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
<IfModule mod_deflate.c>
  # Compress HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Text, XML and Fonts
  AddOutputFilterByType DEFLATE text/html text/plain text/xml text/css text/javascript
  AddOutputFilterByType DEFLATE application/javascript application/x-javascript application/json
  AddOutputFilterByType DEFLATE application/xml application/xhtml+xml application/rss+xml
  AddOutputFilterByType DEFLATE application/vnd.ms-fontobject font/ttf font/otf font/opentype font/woff font/woff2
  AddOutputFilterByType DEFLATE image/svg+xml image/x-icon
</IfModule>

# Ensure CDNs and browsers serve correct compressed versions
<IfModule mod_headers.c>
  Header append Vary User-Agent env=!dont-vary
  Header append Vary Accept-Encoding
</IfModule>

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. BROWSER CACHING & CLS PREVENTATIVE EXPIRES HEADERS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
<IfModule mod_expires.c>
  ExpiresActive On
  ExpiresDefault "access plus 1 month"

  # Force instant layout/schema refresh for web pages (0s revalidation)
  ExpiresByType text/html "access plus 0 seconds"
  ExpiresByType application/xhtml+xml "access plus 0 seconds"

  # Media Assets (Instant loading & high caching)
  ExpiresByType image/jpg "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType image/jpeg "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType image/gif "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType image/png "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType image/webp "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType image/avif "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType image/svg+xml "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType image/x-icon "access plus 1 year"

  # Video / Audio
  ExpiresByType video/mp4 "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType video/mpeg "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType video/webm "access plus 1 year"

  # CSS / JavaScript (Cached to prevent Cumulative Layout Shift / jumping)
  ExpiresByType text/css "access plus 1 month"
  ExpiresByType application/javascript "access plus 1 month"
  ExpiresByType text/javascript "access plus 1 month"

  # Web Fonts (Prevents FOIT / Flash of Unstyled Text)
  ExpiresByType font/ttf "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType font/otf "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType font/woff "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType font/woff2 "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType application/font-woff "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType application/font-woff2 "access plus 1 year"
</IfModule>

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. CACHE-CONTROL, SECURITY & ULTRA-FAST RENDERING HEADERS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
<IfModule mod_headers.c>
  # Eliminate ETag latency issues on load balanced / shared servers
  Header unset ETag
  FileETag None

  # Dynamic Pages: Prevent stale structural/schema caching
  <FilesMatch "\.(html|htm|php)$">
    Header set Cache-Control "max-age=0, no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate"
    Header set Pragma "no-cache"
    Header set Expires "0"
  </FilesMatch>

  # Static Assets: Immutable caching to ensure smooth scrolling & zero lag
  <FilesMatch "\.(ico|pdf|flv|jpg|jpeg|png|gif|js|css|swf|webp|avif|woff|woff2|ttf|otf)$">
    Header set Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
  </FilesMatch>

  # --- Security Headers (Helps Google Trust & Page Security Score) ---
  Header set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
  Header set X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN"
  Header set X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block"
  Header set Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
  
  # Strict-Transport-Security (Forces HTTPS for 1 year)
  Header set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload"
</IfModule>

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. SEARCH ENGINE & AI BOT OPTIMIZATIONS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
<IfModule mod_headers.c>
  # Allow search engine crawlers & AI models (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, GoogleOther) full indexing capability
  Header set X-Robots-Tag "all, max-snippet:-1, max-image-preview:large, max-video-preview:-1"
</IfModule>
</file>

    <script>
      (function(){
        var counters = document.querySelectorAll('#stats-grid [data-target]');
        var started = false;
        function animateCounters(){
          counters.forEach(function(el){
            var target = parseInt(el.getAttribute('data-target'));
            var suffix = el.getAttribute('data-suffix') || '';
            var duration = 1800;
            var start = performance.now();
            function update(now){
              var elapsed = now - start;
              var progress = Math.min(elapsed / duration, 1);
              var ease = 1 - Math.pow(1 - progress, 3);
              el.textContent = Math.floor(ease * target) + suffix;
              if(progress < 1) requestAnimationFrame(update);
            }
            requestAnimationFrame(update);
          });
        }
        var observer = new IntersectionObserver(function(entries){
          if(entries[0].isIntersecting && !started){
            started = true;
            animateCounters();
          }
        }, {threshold: 0.4});
        observer.observe(document.getElementById('stats-grid'));
      })();
    </script>
  </section>

    <script>
      (function(){
        var grid = document.getElementById('story-grid');
        var children = grid.children;
        Array.from(children).forEach(function(el, i){
          el.style.opacity = '0';
          el.style.transform = 'translateY(40px)';
          el.style.transition = 'opacity 1.5s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) '+(i*0.3)+'s, transform 1.5s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) '+(i*0.3)+'s';
        });
        var obs = new IntersectionObserver(function(entries){
          if(entries[0].isIntersecting){
            Array.from(children).forEach(function(el){
              el.style.opacity = '1';
              el.style.transform = 'translateY(0)';
            });
            obs.disconnect();
          }
        }, {threshold: 0.1});
        obs.observe(grid);
      })();
    </script>

        var cards = document.querySelectorAll('.showroom-card');

          entries.forEach(function(entry){
            if(entry.isIntersecting){
              entry.target.style.opacity = '1';
              entry.target.style.transform = 'translateY(0)';
              obs.unobserve(entry.target);
            }
          });
        }, {threshold: 0.15});
        cards.forEach(function(c){ obs.observe(c); });
      })();

    <script>
        $(document).ready(function() {
            // Initialize the phone input setup
            const phoneInput = document.querySelector("#phone");
            const countryHidden = document.querySelector("#country_code");
            const form = document.querySelector("#modern-contact-form");
            let iti = null;

            // CRITICAL SYSTEM FIX: Ensure the hidden country field has a valid form name attribute
            if (countryHidden && !countryHidden.hasAttribute('name')) {
                countryHidden.setAttribute('name', 'country_code');
            }

            if (window.intlTelInput && phoneInput) {
                iti = window.intlTelInput(phoneInput, {
                    initialCountry: "auto",
                    geoIpLookup: function(success, failure) {
                        fetch('https://ipinfo.io/json').then(res => res.json()).then(data => {
                            success(data.country);
                            if(countryHidden) countryHidden.value = data.country.toUpperCase();
                        }).catch(() => {
                            success("ae");
                            if(countryHidden) countryHidden.value = "AE";
                        });
                    },
                    utilsScript: "https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/intl-tel-input/17.0.8/js/utils.js",
                });

                // Listen for manual dial-code/country modifications from the interface list drop-down
                phoneInput.addEventListener('countrychange', function() {
                    if (iti && countryHidden) {
                        const currentCountryData = iti.getSelectedCountryData();
                        if (currentCountryData && currentCountryData.iso2) {
                            countryHidden.value = currentCountryData.iso2.toUpperCase();
                        }
                    }
                });
            }

            // AJAX Form Submission
            $('#modern-contact-form').on('submit', function(e) {
                e.preventDefault();
                var $form = $(this);
                var $btn = $form.find('button[type="submit"]');
                var $toast = $('#form-status-toast');
                
                // Format the phone number to full global string before collecting serialized data
                if (iti && phoneInput) {
                    phoneInput.value = iti.getNumber(); // Overwrites value with full +971500000000 string
                    
                    // Backup check to guarantee code is bound right before compiling dataset
                    const currentCountryData = iti.getSelectedCountryData();
                    if (countryHidden && currentCountryData && currentCountryData.iso2) {
                        countryHidden.value = currentCountryData.iso2.toUpperCase();
                    }
                }

                $btn.addClass('btn-loading').prop('disabled', true);
                $toast.hide(); 
                
                $.ajax({
                    type: 'POST',
                    url: $form.attr('action'),
                    data: $form.serialize(), // Now properly bundles name="country_code" into the raw string payload
                    success: function(response) {
                        $btn.removeClass('btn-loading').prop('disabled', false);
                        var cleanResponse = response.trim();
                        
                        if (cleanResponse === "success") {
                            showToast("✓ Thank you! Your message has been sent successfully.", "success");
                            $form[0].reset(); 
                            setTimeout(function(){ location.reload(); }, 2000); // Reload to get fresh captcha
                        } else if (cleanResponse === "invalid_captcha") {
                            showToast("✕ Incorrect Captcha answer. Please try again.", "error");
                        } else {
                            showToast("✕ Error: " + cleanResponse, "error");
                        }
                    },
                    error: function(xhr, status, error) {
                        $btn.removeClass('btn-loading').prop('disabled', false);
                        showToast("✕ Connection Failed: " + error, "error");
                    }
                });
            });

            function showToast(message, type) {
                var $toast = $('#form-status-toast');
                $toast.text(message)
                    .removeClass('toast-success toast-error')
                    .addClass('toast-' + type)
                    .fadeIn();
                var timeout = (type === 'error') ? 7000 : 5000;
                setTimeout(function() { $toast.fadeOut(); }, timeout);
            }
        });
    </script>
</body>
</html>
</file>

<file path="send-mail.php">
<?php 
session_start();

use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\PHPMailer;
use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception;

// Load sensitive configuration settings
$config = require __DIR__ . '/includes/config.php';

// 1. Path Management: Ensure these files exist in your /PHPMailer/src/ directory
require __DIR__ . '/PHPMailer/src/Exception.php';
require __DIR__ . '/PHPMailer/src/PHPMailer.php';
require __DIR__ . '/PHPMailer/src/SMTP.php';

// --- Server-Side Captcha Validation ---
if ($_SERVER["REQUEST_METHOD"] == "POST") {
    $user_captcha = isset($_POST['captcha_input']) ? trim($_POST['captcha_input']) : '';
    $correct_captcha = isset($_SESSION['captcha_answer']) ? $_SESSION['captcha_answer'] : null;

    if ($correct_captcha === null || $user_captcha === '' || (int)$user_captcha !== (int)$correct_captcha) {
        echo "invalid_captcha";
        exit;
    }
}

$mail = new PHPMailer(true);

try {
    // --- Server Settings ---
    $mail->isSMTP();
    $mail->Host       = $config['smtp']['host'];
    $mail->SMTPAuth   = $config['smtp']['auth'];
    
    // SECURITY NOTE: Credentials loaded from includes/config.php
    $mail->Username   = $config['smtp']['username'];
    $mail->Password   = $config['smtp']['password']; 
    
    $mail->SMTPSecure = PHPMailer::ENCRYPTION_SMTPS; 
    $mail->Port       = $config['smtp']['port'];

    // --- SSL Configuration ---
    // Keep this only for local testing (XAMPP). 
    // Remove the 'SMTPOptions' block entirely when moving to a live Linux server.
    $mail->SMTPOptions = array(
        'ssl' => array(
            'verify_peer' => false,
            'verify_peer_name' => false,
            'allow_self_signed' => true
        )
    );

    // --- Recipients ---
    $mail->setFrom($config['mail']['from_email'], $config['mail']['from_name']);
    $mail->addAddress($config['mail']['to_email']); 
    // $mail->addCC($config['mail']['from_email']);
    
    // --- Data Sanitization (Fixing XSS & Injection) ---
    // Mandatory Fields (Name, Email, Phone, Subject)
    $name    = isset($_POST['name']) ? htmlspecialchars(strip_tags(trim($_POST['name']))) : 'No Name';
    $email   = filter_var($_POST['email'] ?? '', FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL) ? $_POST['email'] : 'Invalid Email';
    $phone   = isset($_POST['phone']) ? htmlspecialchars(strip_tags(trim($_POST['phone']))) : 'No Phone';
    
    // Fallback support for subject (Case insensitive check)
    $subject_input = $_POST['Subject'] ?? $_POST['subject'] ?? '';
    $subject = !empty($subject_input) ? htmlspecialchars(strip_tags(trim($subject_input))) : 'New Website Inquiry';
    
    // Optional Field: Message (No error thrown if empty)
    $raw_message = isset($_POST['message']) ? trim($_POST['message']) : '';
    $message = !empty($raw_message) ? htmlspecialchars(strip_tags($raw_message)) : 'N/A';
    
    // Extra tracking parameters captured by intl-tel-input
    $country_code = isset($_POST['country_code']) ? htmlspecialchars(strip_tags(trim($_POST['country_code']))) : '';

    // Mandatory Validation: Don't send if email, name, or phone is invalid/empty
    if ($email === 'Invalid Email') {
        throw new Exception("Please provide a valid email address.");
    }

    if (empty($name) || $name === 'No Name') {
        throw new Exception("Please provide your name.");
    }

    if (empty($phone) || $phone === 'No Phone') {
        throw new Exception("Please provide your phone number.");
    }

    // Set reply-to header so clicking "Reply" responds directly to the user
    $mail->addReplyTo($email, $name);

    // --- Email Content ---
    $mail->isHTML(true);
    $mail->Subject = "New Contact form Inquiry from website theyyampattilgcc.com: " . $subject;
    
    // HTML Email Body
    $mail->Body = "
        <h3>New contact form enquiry from website theyyampattilgcc.com</h3>
        <p><strong>Name:</strong> {$name}</p>
        <p><strong>Email:</strong> {$email}</p>
        <p><strong>Phone:</strong> {$phone} " . (!empty($country_code) ? "({$country_code})" : "") . "</p>
        <p><strong>Subject:</strong> {$subject}</p>
        <p><strong>Message:</strong><br>" . nl2br($message) . "</p>
    ";
    
    // Plain text version for non-HTML mail clients
    $mail->AltBody = "Name: $name\nEmail: $email\nPhone: $phone " . (!empty($country_code) ? "($country_code)" : "") . "\nSubject: $subject\nMessage: $message";

    $mail->send();
    
    // Clear the evaluated captcha answer out of session memory upon a clean send
    unset($_SESSION['captcha_answer']);
    unset($_SESSION['captcha_num1']);
    unset($_SESSION['captcha_num2']);
    unset($_SESSION['captcha_operator']);
    
    echo "success";

} catch (Exception $e) {
    // Return error response for AJAX handler
    echo "Message could not be sent. Mailer Error: {$mail->ErrorInfo}";
}
?>
</file>

    <script>
        // Smooth Responsive Accordion Logic
        document.querySelectorAll('.accrodion-title').forEach(title => {
            title.addEventListener('click', () => {
                const parent = title.parentElement;
                const wasActive = parent.classList.contains('active');
                
                document.querySelectorAll('.accrodion').forEach(acc => {
                    acc.classList.remove('active');
                    const btn = acc.querySelector('.accrodion-title');
                    if (btn) btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
                });
                
                if (!wasActive) {
                    parent.classList.add('active');
                    title.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
                }
            });
        });
    </script>

    <script>
        // High Performance Non-Jumping FAQ Accordion
        document.querySelectorAll('.faq-question').forEach(button => {
            button.addEventListener('click', () => {
                const faqItem = button.parentElement;
                const isOpen = faqItem.classList.contains('active');

                document.querySelectorAll('.faq-item').forEach(item => {
                    item.classList.remove('active');
                    item.querySelector('.faq-question').setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
                });

                if (!isOpen) {
                    faqItem.classList.add('active');
                    button.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
                }
            });
        });
    </script>
